scope.en: Princeton Rights, Rules, Responsibilities 2.4; Scholarly Integrity guidance; Office of the Dean of the College course policies; McGraw Center teaching guidance; OIT Generative AI Tools Use Policy (Aug 2026) and AI tools directory; Department of Art and Archaeology independent-work policy. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 普林斯顿《权利、规则与责任》2.4；学术诚信指引；本科学院院长办公室课程规定；McGraw 教学中心指引；OIT《生成式 AI 工具使用政策》（2026 年 8 月）及工具目录；艺术与考古学系独立研究政策。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: Whether, when and how generative AI may be used is set by each instructor and stated in the syllabus; students must follow course and departmental policies. Directly copying output, passing off AI output (including reworded or paraphrased output) as your own, or exceeding the instructor's limits is an academic integrity violation. Some departments are stricter: Art and Archaeology bans AI text generation, drafting and editing in coursework unless an instructor grants a disclosed exception.
coursework.zh: 是否、何时及如何使用生成式 AI 由各课程教师决定并写入课程大纲；学生须遵守课程和院系规定。直接复制输出、把 AI 输出（包括改写或意译后的输出）当作自己的成果，或超出教师限定范围，均构成学术诚信违规。部分院系更严格：艺术与考古学系禁止在课程作业中用 AI 生成、起草或润色文字，除非教师书面准许并要求披露的例外。
coursework.meaningEn: Course-by-course permission under RRR 2.4 and ODOC course policy; department rules may be stricter.
coursework.meaningZh: 依《权利、规则与责任》2.4 和课程规定逐门课决定；院系规则可能更严。

exams.en: No university-wide AI permission applies to examinations. Undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots, when completing quizzes or examinations or any work for an academic requirement, and exceeding the instructor's parameters is a violation. Art and Archaeology prohibits AI text generation in final examinations.
exams.zh: 考试没有全校性的 AI 使用许可。本科生在完成测验、考试或任何学业要求的作业时，不得使用普林斯顿以外的辅导资源，包括 AI 辅导机器人；超出教师规定范围即属违规。艺术与考古学系禁止在期末考试中用 AI 生成文字。
exams.meaningEn: Exam use follows the instructor; AI tutoring bots are barred for undergraduate graded work.
exams.meaningZh: 考试使用遵循教师规定；本科计分作业禁用 AI 辅导机器人。

disclosure.en: When an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite it, because AI is not a source. Failing to disclose, including AI used for rewording, paraphrasing or editing, is a scholarly integrity violation even in courses where AI is allowed. Instructors may supply a disclosure template; otherwise the University template asks which tool was used, for what purpose, and confirms records were kept.
disclosure.zh: 教师允许使用生成式 AI 时，学生必须进行披露，而不是把 AI 当作来源引用，因为 AI 不是来源。即使在允许 AI 的课程中，未披露（包括用 AI 改写、意译或润色）也属于学术诚信违规。教师可提供披露模板；否则可使用学校模板，说明所用工具、用途并确认保留了使用记录。
disclosure.meaningEn: Disclosure of permitted use is mandatory (RRR 2.4.7).
disclosure.meaningZh: 获准使用后的披露为强制要求（RRR 2.4.7）。

privacy_data.en: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy covers administrative and operational University information (student, financial, HR records), not information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. For that information, Internal or Confidential data may only go into University-licensed AI tools, never into public AI tools, and Restricted data must not be used with any AI tool. Research and teaching data follow their own rules.
privacy_data.zh: 普林斯顿《生成式 AI 工具使用政策》适用于学校行政与运营信息（学生、财务、人事记录），不包括用于研究、学术或教学的信息。对这类信息，内部或机密数据只能输入学校许可的 AI 工具，不得输入公共 AI 工具；受限数据不得用于任何 AI 工具。研究和教学数据另有规定。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Data-class rules for administrative information (OIT policy, Aug 2026).
privacy_data.meaningZh: 行政信息的数据分级规则（OIT 政策，2026 年 8 月）。

approved_tools.en: OIT lists Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Adobe Creative Cloud image generation for faculty, students and staff without a request. Other tools (Claude/Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Gemini Workspace+, Gemini Notebook, the AI Sandbox) are for faculty and those they sponsor, Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium is faculty-only, and Zoom AI is a faculty/staff pilot; these require a request and the directory marks a cost. Tools are approved for Public, Internal and Confidential data, not Restricted. Access is not permission to use a tool in a course.
approved_tools.zh: OIT 目录列出 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat 和 Adobe Creative Cloud 图像生成，教师、学生和员工无需申请即可使用。其他工具（Claude/Claude Code、GitHub Copilot、Gemini Workspace+、Gemini Notebook、AI Sandbox）面向教师及其担保人员，Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium 仅限教师，Zoom AI 为教职员工试点；这些需申请，目录标注涉及费用。工具获准处理公开、内部和机密数据，不含受限数据。能使用工具不等于课程允许使用。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Current OIT Princeton-supported AI Tools directory.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 现行 OIT 支持工具目录。

research_publication.en: There is no single university-wide AI rule for theses in the reviewed sources; independent work follows department policy. Art and Archaeology never allows exceptions for the junior paper or senior thesis. Research AI tools such as the AI Sandbox and Claude are available to faculty and those they sponsor for research use.
research_publication.zh: 所审核来源中没有统一适用于全校毕业论文的 AI 规则；独立研究遵循院系政策。艺术与考古学系对初级论文（junior paper）和毕业论文（senior thesis）一律不设例外。AI Sandbox 和 Claude 等研究工具面向教师及其担保人员用于研究。
research_publication.meaningEn: Independent work follows department policy; research tools are faculty-sponsored.
research_publication.meaningZh: 独立研究依院系政策；研究工具需教师担保。

academic_integrity.en: Undisclosed AI use, passing off AI output as your own and exceeding permitted use are academic integrity violations under Rights, Rules, Responsibilities. Undergraduates may not use AI tutoring bots for graded work. The McGraw Center recommends against using AI detectors to decide whether a policy was violated. Discipline procedures and penalties are set by the separate Honor Committee and Committee on Discipline processes and were not re-verified in this review.
academic_integrity.zh: 根据《权利、规则与责任》，未披露的 AI 使用、把 AI 输出当作自己的成果以及超出许可范围使用均属学术诚信违规。本科生不得在计分作业中使用 AI 辅导机器人。McGraw 中心建议不要用 AI 检测工具判断是否违规。纪律程序和处分由荣誉委员会与纪律委员会分别处理，本次未重新核实。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: RRR 2.4 integrity rules; procedures not re-verified.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: RRR 2.4 诚信规则；程序未重新核实。

topicBasis.coursework: Whether, when and how generative AI may be used is set by each instructor and stated in the syllabus; students must follow course and departmental policies. Directly copying output, passing off AI output (including reworded or paraphrased output) as your own, or exceeding the instructor's limits is an academic integrity violation. Some departments are stricter: Art and Archaeology bans AI text generation, drafting and editing in coursework unless an instructor grants a disclosed exception.
topicBasis.exams: No university-wide AI permission applies to examinations. Undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots, when completing quizzes or examinations or any work for an academic requirement, and exceeding the instructor's parameters is a violation. Art and Archaeology prohibits AI text generation in final examinations.
topicBasis.disclosure: When an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite it, because AI is not a source. Failing to disclose, including AI used for rewording, paraphrasing or editing, is a scholarly integrity violation even in courses where AI is allowed. Instructors may supply a disclosure template; otherwise the University template asks which tool was used, for what purpose, and confirms records were kept.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy covers administrative and operational University information (student, financial, HR records), not information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. For that information, Internal or Confidential data may only go into University-licensed AI tools, never into public AI tools, and Restricted data must not be used with any AI tool. Research and teaching data follow their own rules.
topicBasis.approved_tools: OIT lists Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Adobe Creative Cloud image generation for faculty, students and staff without a request. Other tools (Claude/Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Gemini Workspace+, Gemini Notebook, the AI Sandbox) are for faculty and those they sponsor, Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium is faculty-only, and Zoom AI is a faculty/staff pilot; these require a request and the directory marks a cost. Tools are approved for Public, Internal and Confidential data, not Restricted. Access is not permission to use a tool in a course.
topicBasis.research_publication: There is no single university-wide AI rule for theses in the reviewed sources; independent work follows department policy. Art and Archaeology never allows exceptions for the junior paper or senior thesis. Research AI tools such as the AI Sandbox and Claude are available to faculty and those they sponsor for research use.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Undisclosed AI use, passing off AI output as your own and exceeding permitted use are academic integrity violations under Rights, Rules, Responsibilities. Undergraduates may not use AI tutoring bots for graded work. The McGraw Center recommends against using AI detectors to decide whether a policy was violated. Discipline procedures and penalties are set by the separate Honor Committee and Committee on Discipline processes and were not re-verified in this review.

do.en: Check each course syllabus and your department's policy before using AI; Art and Archaeology bans AI writing help unless an instructor grants a disclosed exception (never for the junior paper or senior thesis).
do.zh: 使用 AI 前查看每门课程大纲和所在院系政策；艺术与考古学系禁止 AI 写作辅助，除非教师书面准许并要求披露的例外（初级论文和毕业论文从无例外）。

do.en: When AI is permitted, disclose it (not cite it), including use for rewording, paraphrasing or editing, and keep records of your use.
do.zh: 获准使用 AI 时须披露（而非引用），包括用于改写、意译或润色的情况，并保留使用记录。

do.en: Use University-licensed tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with your Princeton login when working with non-public information.
do.zh: 处理非公开信息时，使用学校许可的工具（如用普林斯顿账号登录的 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat）。

dont.en: Do not copy AI output or submit reworded AI text as your own, and do not exceed what your instructor allows.
dont.zh: 不要复制 AI 输出或把改写后的 AI 文字当作自己的成果提交，也不要超出教师允许的范围。

dont.en: Undergraduates: do not use AI tutoring bots or other non-Princeton tutoring when completing homework, problem sets, quizzes or exams.
dont.zh: 本科生：完成作业、习题、测验或考试时，不要使用 AI 辅导机器人或其他非普林斯顿辅导资源。

dont.en: Do not put Restricted data into any AI tool, or non-public Princeton data into public AI tools.
dont.zh: 不要把受限数据输入任何 AI 工具，也不要把非公开的普林斯顿数据输入公共 AI 工具。

CL-001.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4) states that generative AI is not a source; where an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge it. Disclosure of permitted use is therefore required, not merely recommended, while whether AI may be used at all is set by the course or department. Scholarly Integrity guidance says failure to disclose, even in a course where AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation, and offers a disclosure template.

evidence.quote: Generative AI is not a source as defined in this provision because its output is not created by a person. If generative AI is permitted by the instructor, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge the use, since it is an algorithm rather than a source.
evidence.location: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 178-178 of captured page text

evidence.quote: All the tenets of scholarly integrity apply to use of generative AI: students must not pass off any output by generative AI as their own, and so a failure of disclosure, even in a course where generative AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation.
evidence.location: How to disclose generative AI; lines 86-86 of captured page text

CL-002.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities states that students must adhere to course and departmental generative AI policies, and that inappropriate uses on work submitted for an academic requirement - directly copying output, representing AI output as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing it), exceeding the instructor's parameters, or failing to disclose use (including use for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) - constitute academic integrity violations.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for adhering to course and departmental policies regarding the use of generative AI. Inappropriate uses of generative AI on any work submitted to fulfill an academic requirement, such as directly copying the output, representing output generated by or derived from generative AI as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing output from generative AI and representing it as their own), exceeding the parameters of use specified by the instructor, or failing to disclose its use (including the use of generative AI for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) constitute violations of academic integrity.
evidence.location: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 143-143 of captured page text

CL-003.text: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy (last updated August 2026) governs Princeton administrative and operational information, including student, financial and HR information; it expressly excludes information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. Under it, only University-licensed generative AI tools should be used with University Information classified as Internal or Confidential, publicly available generative AI tools may not be used with such information, and even University-licensed tools should not be used with Restricted information. It is not a blanket rule covering all student coursework or research data.

evidence.quote: The purpose of this policy is to manage the use of Princeton University administrative and operational information with generative AI tools.
evidence.location: Purpose; lines 82-82 of captured page text

evidence.quote: For the purposes of this policy, University Information does not include information used for research, academic or instructional purposes.
evidence.location: Scope; lines 90-90 of captured page text

evidence.quote: University-licensed generative AI tools should be used with Princeton Information classified as Internal or Confidential under the University’s Information Security Policy
evidence.location: Policy; lines 190-190 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The use of publicly available generative AI tools in conjunction with such Princeton Information is not permitted by the University. University-licensed generative AI tools should not be used with Princeton Information classified as Restricted.
evidence.location: Policy; lines 100-100 of captured page text

CL-004.text: Princeton's Office of the Dean of the College requires faculty to set clear expectations for whether, when and how generative AI can be used and to state them in the course syllabus; all students are expected to disclose their generative AI use and not pass off AI-generated content as their own, and faculty may provide their own disclosure template or use the standard one.

evidence.quote: Faculty must set clear expectations for whether, when, and how generative AI can be used and state those expectations in the course syllabus. Work created with the assistance of AI tools should never be a proxy for original work. All students are expected to abide by scholarly integrity expectations for appropriate generative AI use, which include disclosing their use of generative AI and not passing off AI-generated content as their own work.
evidence.location: Students and Generative AI; lines 212-212 of captured page text

CL-005.text: Princeton's McGraw Center for Teaching and Learning recommends against using AI detection tools to determine whether students have violated an instructor's AI policy. This is teaching guidance, not a disciplinary evidence rule.

evidence.quote: We recommend against using AI detection tools to determine if students have violated your AI policy.
evidence.location: Scholarly Integrity and Detecting the Use of AI; lines 179-179 of captured page text

CL-007.text: Princeton's Dean of the College stated in the Fall 2023 memo that the decision to allow, limit or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work remains with the faculty. This is consistent with current course-procedure guidance requiring faculty to state their expectations in the syllabus; the 2023 memo is historical context rather than the current governing text.

evidence.quote: First and foremost, the decision to allow, limit, or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work will remain our faculty’s. Faculty members have the discretion to set their own generative AI policy for their courses.
evidence.location: Fall 2023 memo; lines 108-108 of captured page text

draft-claim-princeton-ai-tutoring-bots.text: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4.5), as quoted by Scholarly Integrity, provides that undergraduates may use only Princeton-authorized academic support: when completing any work to fulfil an academic requirement (homework, problem sets, quizzes or examinations), undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots. This applies to work done for academic requirements; it is not a ban on all AI-assisted study.

evidence.quote: When completing any work to fulfill an academic requirement (such as homework assignments, problem sets, quizzes or examinations of any kind), undergraduate students may not make use of any non-Princeton tutoring resources, including paid or unpaid tutors, independent tutoring services, or AI tutoring bots.

draft-claim-princeton-art-archaeology-in.text: Princeton's Department of Art and Archaeology prohibits using AI as a text-generation tool in coursework, final examinations and independent projects: students may not submit AI-generated text, use AI-generated text as a draft they then modify or paraphrase, or use generative AI to edit and revise their work. Instructors may grant exceptions for a course assignment with written disclosure, but exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or senior thesis. This department rule is stricter than general course-by-course permission.

evidence.quote: As a result, the Department of Art & Archaeology explicitly prohibits the use of AI as a text-generation tool in the writing of coursework, final examinations, and independent projects alike.
evidence.location: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text

evidence.quote: A student may not rely on AI-generated text as a rough or partial draft, which they then modify or paraphrase before submitting it as their own work; likewise, a student may not use generative AI in editing and revising their work.

evidence.quote: That said, an instructor may wish to grant exceptions for AI use in a course assignment as long as the student strictly follows the instructor’s guidelines and discloses the specific use in writing. Exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or the senior thesis.

scope.en: University of Sydney student AI guidance (updated 2 June 2026); academic integrity, investigation and appeals pages; Graduate Research HDR AI guidance; Teaching@Sydney assessment framework; ChatGPT Edu and Student IT pages. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 悉尼大学学生 AI 指引（2026 年 6 月 2 日更新）；学术诚信、调查与申诉页面；研究生院 HDR AI 指引；Teaching@Sydney 考核框架；ChatGPT Edu 与学生 IT 页面。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: Each unit outline has a 'Use of AI' column for every assessment. AI can be used in open (unsupervised) assessments, where educators guide appropriate use and use must be acknowledged; it generally cannot be used in secure (supervised) assessments unless the unit coordinator expressly permits it. These coursework rules do not apply to HDR theses.
coursework.zh: 每门课程大纲都有“Use of AI”一栏，逐项标明各考核能否使用 AI。开放式（无监督）考核可以使用 AI，由教师指导适当用法且须声明；安全（有监督）考核一般不得使用，除非课程负责人明确许可。上述课程规则不适用于研究型学位（HDR）论文。
coursework.meaningEn: Open/secure assessment lanes and the unit outline 'Use of AI' column.
coursework.meaningZh: 开放/安全两类考核及课程大纲“Use of AI”栏。

exams.en: Secure (supervised) assessments, such as secure exams, generally prohibit AI unless the unit coordinator gives express permission in the unit outline; using AI where prohibited can breach the Academic Integrity Policy.
exams.zh: 安全（有监督）考核（如安全考试）一般禁止使用 AI，除非课程负责人在大纲中明确许可；在禁止的情况下使用 AI 可能违反《学术诚信政策》。
exams.meaningEn: Secure assessment rule.
exams.meaningZh: 安全考核规则。

disclosure.en: AI used in assessments must be acknowledged, including AI translation, paraphrasing or referencing tools; basic spelling/grammar correction and word processing are exempt. The statement gives the tool name and version, publisher, URL and how it was used; coordinators may require logs. HDR theses must include an AI statement even if no AI was used.
disclosure.zh: 在考核中使用 AI 必须声明，包括 AI 翻译、改写或参考文献工具；文字处理和基础拼写语法纠正除外。声明须写明工具名称和版本、发布方、网址及用途；课程负责人可要求提交使用记录。研究型学位论文即使未使用 AI 也须附 AI 声明。
disclosure.meaningEn: Acknowledgement content and HDR thesis statement.
disclosure.meaningZh: 声明内容与 HDR 论文声明。

privacy_data.en: Do not enter confidential, personal, proprietary or otherwise sensitive information into AI tools. Inputting University teaching or course materials, other students' work, external partners' intellectual property or anyone's personal or health information counts as misuse. HDR students must never upload personal, sensitive or confidential information to any AI tool.
privacy_data.zh: 不得向 AI 工具输入机密、个人、专有或其他敏感信息。输入学校教学或课程材料、其他学生的作品、外部合作方知识产权或任何人的个人或健康信息均属不当使用。研究型学位学生不得向任何 AI 工具上传个人、敏感或机密信息。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Guardrails and misuse examples.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 使用底线与不当使用示例。

approved_tools.en: Microsoft Copilot Chat is free for all students and is the go-to option when signed in via Okta (only some highly protected data). Cogniti agents are provided through units; Harvey AI is for Sydney Law School students only. ChatGPT Edu is not yet generally available: a student pilot is planned for October 2026 and release to all students in Semester 1 2027, with agents and connectors assessed before enabling. Tool access does not override an assessment's AI rules.
approved_tools.zh: Microsoft Copilot Chat 对全体学生免费，经 Okta 登录后为首选工具（仅限部分高度受保护数据）。Cogniti 智能体由课程提供；Harvey AI 仅供悉尼法学院学生使用。ChatGPT Edu 尚未全面开放：计划 2026 年 10 月开展学生试点，2027 年第一学期向全体学生推出，智能体和连接器需先评估后开启。能使用工具不改变考核的 AI 规则。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Student AI tools list and ChatGPT Edu rollout.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 学生 AI 工具列表与 ChatGPT Edu 推出计划。

research_publication.en: HDR (research degree) students may use AI for spelling and grammar but not to generate content, rewrite drafts' academic language or include AI output as substantive thesis content, unless AI is integral to the approved research methodology (supervisor approval and ethics arrangements). Theses need an AI statement and students should keep prompts and outputs.
research_publication.zh: 研究型学位（HDR）学生可用 AI 改进拼写和语法，但不得用于生成内容、上传草稿润色学术语言或把 AI 输出作为论文实质内容，除非 AI 是经导师批准并纳入伦理审批的研究方法组成部分。论文须附 AI 声明，并应保留提示词和输出记录。
research_publication.meaningEn: Graduate Research HDR rules.
research_publication.meaningZh: 研究生院 HDR 规则。

academic_integrity.en: Inappropriately generating content with AI is an academic integrity breach and AI-generated submissions may be treated as contract cheating. Turnitin's AI detector may be used, but its score is never the only evidence. Minor breaches may be handled by the unit coordinator, more serious ones by the faculty Educational Integrity team, and the most serious by the Registrar. Academic decisions: faculty/Academic Panel review within 20 working days, then SAB within 15 working days; Registrar misconduct penalties: SDAC appeal within 20 working days.
academic_integrity.zh: 不当使用 AI 生成内容属于学术诚信违规，AI 生成的提交物可被视为代写。可使用 Turnitin AI 检测，但其分数绝不是唯一证据。轻微违规可由课程负责人处理，较严重的由学院教育诚信团队处理，最严重的由教务长（Registrar）处理。学术决定：20 个工作日内申请学院/学术小组复核，之后 15 个工作日内向学生申诉机构（SAB）申诉；教务长作出的纪律处分：20 个工作日内向学生纪律申诉委员会（SDAC）申诉。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Integrity breaches, investigation levels and appeal routes.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 违规认定、调查层级与申诉路径。

Turnitin's AI detector may be used, but its score is never the only evidence. Minor breaches may be handled by the unit coordinator, more serious ones by the faculty Educational Integrity team, and the most serious by the Registrar. Academic decisions: faculty/Academic Panel review within 20 working days, then SAB within 15 working days; Registrar misconduct penalties: SDAC appeal within 20 working days.

do.en: Check the 'Use of AI' column in your unit outline for each assessment: open assessments allow AI with acknowledgement; secure ones generally do not.
do.zh: 查看课程大纲中每项考核的“Use of AI”栏：开放式考核允许使用 AI 并须声明；安全考核一般不允许。

do.en: Acknowledge AI use with the tool name and version, publisher, URL and how you used it; spelling/grammar-only tools are exempt.
do.zh: 声明 AI 使用时写明工具名称与版本、发布方、网址和用途；仅纠正拼写语法的工具无需声明。

do.en: HDR students: include an AI statement in your thesis (even if you used none) and keep your prompts and outputs.
do.zh: 研究型学位学生：论文须附 AI 声明（即使未使用），并保留提示词和输出记录。

dont.en: Do not use AI in secure assessments unless the unit outline expressly allows it.
dont.zh: 除非课程大纲明确允许，不要在安全考核中使用 AI。

dont.en: Do not input course materials, other students' work, or personal or health information into AI tools.
dont.zh: 不要把课程材料、其他学生的作品或个人、健康信息输入 AI 工具。

dont.en: HDR students: do not use AI to generate thesis content or polish a draft's academic language unless it is part of your approved methodology.
dont.zh: 研究型学位学生：除非属于获批的研究方法，不要用 AI 生成论文内容或润色草稿学术语言。

cl-the-university-of-sydney-microsoft-co.text: The University of Sydney Student IT page describes Microsoft Copilot as a University-endorsed GenAI tool, free for all students and accessed by signing in with a University account; students may use it for assessments provided they use AI tools responsibly, which still depends on each assessment's AI rules.

evidence.quote: Microsoft Copilot is a University endorsed GenAI tool and is free for all students. You're welcome to use it for assessments provided you are aware of how to use AI tools responsibly.
evidence.location: Microsoft Copilot; lines 172-172 of captured page text

draft-claim-usyd-academic-appeal-routes.text: University of Sydney academic decisions and misconduct findings use different review routes. For academic decisions, students may apply for faculty or Academic Panel review within 20 working days, and may appeal to the Student Appeals Body (SAB) within 15 working days of the review outcome, but not simply because they disagree with it. Where the Registrar makes a misconduct finding or penalty, the student may appeal to the Student Disciplinary Appeals Committee (SDAC) within 20 working days of the penalty notice. Not every AI-related academic integrity matter is a Registrar misconduct decision.

evidence.quote:
If an informal resolution doesn’t resolve your concerns, the next level available to you is to apply for a review from the relevant faculty or administrative unit.
You must apply within 20 working days of receiving:
evidence.location: Level 2; lines 81-83 of captured page text

evidence.quote: If you apply for a SAB appeal, you must apply within 15 working days of receiving the outcome of your faculty or Academic Panel review. If you are granted an extension, you must apply within the extended timeframe.
evidence.location: Level 3; lines 101-101 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You cannot appeal to the SAB simply because you disagree with the faculty or Academic Panel review outcome.
evidence.location: Level 3; lines 97-97 of captured page text

evidence.quote: To be eligible for a disciplinary appeal, you will need to submit your appeal within 20 working days of receiving your penalty notice from the Registrar.
evidence.location: Appealing a misconduct outcome; lines 29-29 of captured page text

draft-claim-usyd-ai-tools-cogniti-harvey.text: Besides Copilot, the University of Sydney lists Cogniti (designed by University educators), Harvey AI (available to all Sydney Law School students, a faculty-specific legal tool) and ChatGPT Edu. ChatGPT Edu is not yet available to all students: a student pilot is planned for October 2026 and release to all students is scheduled for Semester 1 2027. Custom GPTs, agents, plugins and connectors are individually assessed before being enabled. Its data are stored in Australia at rest, with globally routed inference.

evidence.quote: Designed by University of Sydney educators, Cogniti assists student learning in interactive and context-sensitive ways.
evidence.location: AI tools you can use: Cogniti; lines 149-149 of captured page text

evidence.quote: All University of Sydney Law School students have access to Harvey AI, a legal-specialist AI tool used across the profession.
evidence.location: AI tools you can use: Harvey AI; lines 169-169 of captured page text

evidence.quote: A student pilot of ChatGPT Edu is planned for October 2026, around the time of the staff release of the tool. Following the pilot, ChatGPT Edu is scheduled for release to all students in Semester 1 2027.
evidence.location: When will students get access?; lines 47-47 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Additional capabilities such as custom GPTs, agents, plugins, connectors and other advanced features will be individually assessed before being enabled.
evidence.location: What features are included?; lines 57-57 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The University of Sydney's ChatGPT Edu workspace has Australian data residency at rest and globally routed inference.
evidence.location: Data residency; lines 111-111 of captured page text

draft-claim-usyd-hdr-genai-rules.text: Higher degree by research (HDR) students at the University of Sydney do not inherit the open-assessment AI permission. The Graduate Research guidance says generative AI may in general be used to improve spelling or grammar (spelling/grammar checkers and reference managers are permitted) but not to generate content; prompting AI to generate written or other content, uploading a draft to improve its academic language, and incorporating AI outputs as substantive thesis content are prohibited, except where AI is integral to the research design or methodology and approved by the supervisor and through the ethics arrangements. HDR students should never enter personal, sensitive or confidential information into any gen AI tool.

evidence.quote: In general terms, gen AI tools may be used where, for example, they assist in improving the spelling or grammar of your writing, but not where they generate content for you.
evidence.location: Use of generative AI: General overview; lines 316-316 of captured page text

evidence.quote: However, inputting prompts into a gen AI tool (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, etc.) to generate written or other content; uploading a draft of your work into a gen AI tool to improve the academic language or any other aspect of your work; and/or incorporating gen AI outputs as substantive content in your thesis or other submitted work are all prohibited, except under certain circumstances as outlined under ‘Responsible use of generative AI in research’.
evidence.location: Use of generative AI: General overview; lines 320-320 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The responsible use of gen AI tools may be permitted when it is integral to your research design or methodology and its use has been approved by your supervisor.
evidence.location: Responsible use of generative AI in research; lines 324-324 of captured page text

evidence.quote: If you are considering using any form of gen AI or gen AI-assisted technology as part of your research methodology or in ways integral to your research project, you must check with your supervisor first to confirm whether this is permitted.  Then it should be approved as part of your ethics arrangements.
evidence.location: Responsible use of generative AI in research; lines 326-326 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Never enter or upload any personal, sensitive or confidential information into any gen AI tool.
evidence.location: Be mindful of the information you enter or upload; lines 340-340 of captured page text

draft-claim-usyd-hdr-thesis-ai-statement.text: All University of Sydney theses should contain a statement acknowledging any use of generative AI, and if no generative AI was used the thesis should still include a statement to that effect. HDR students who use generative AI in their research or thesis should document all prompts and keep records of generated outputs.

evidence.quote: All theses should contain an acknowledgement section, an author attribution statement and a statement that acknowledges any use of generative artificial intelligence (AI).
evidence.location: Thesis content; lines 201-201 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Any generative AI tools that you have used in your research or in any part of the preparation of your thesis should be acknowledged. If you did not use generative AI, then you should still include a statement to this effect.
evidence.location: Generative AI statement; lines 352-352 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You should also document (such as by taking screenshots of) all prompts that you input into any gen AI tool, and keep records of all generated outputs.
evidence.location: Guidelines for acknowledging use of gen AI; lines 356-356 of captured page text

draft-claim-usyd-integrity-investigation.text: At the University of Sydney, minor academic integrity breaches may be handled locally by unit coordinators, more serious ones are investigated by the faculty Educational Integrity team, and the most serious suspected cheating is handled by the Registrar under the Student Discipline Rule. Students may bring a support person to an integrity meeting.

evidence.quote: Some minor breaches can be handled by unit coordinators locally while more serious breaches are referred to the relevant faculty’s Educational Integrity Coordinator or one of its nominated academics for investigation.
evidence.location: Who investigates; lines 32-32 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The most serious instances of suspected cheating are handled under the misconduct process, which is governed by the University of Sydney (Student Discipline) Rule and handled by the Registrar.
evidence.location: Who investigates; lines 34-34 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You can bring a support person, and occasionally your teacher or examination invigilator (supervisor) will also be asked to attend.
evidence.location: Meetings; lines 106-106 of captured page text

usyd-claim-1.text: The University of Sydney's Academic Integrity Policy 2022 states it is an academic integrity breach to inappropriately generate content using artificial intelligence to complete an assessment task, and submitting an assessment generated by AI may be considered contract cheating.

evidence.quote: Clause 4(9)(2)(j)(i) states that it is an academic integrity breach to inappropriately generate content using artificial intelligence to complete an assessment task. Clause 4(13)(1)(i) states that submitting an assessment generated by AI may be considered contract cheating.
evidence.location: The policy and assessment frameworks section, 'What is in the policy about generative AI use by students?'

usyd-claim-10.text: The University of Sydney Assessment Procedures state that unit of study coordinators will specify if, and which, artificial intelligence tools are permitted for each assessment and how their use must be acknowledged.

evidence.quote: Unit of study coordinators will specify if, and which, artificial intelligence (AI) tools are permitted for each assessment and how their use must be acknowledged.
evidence.location: Quick guide, 'Can I use automated writing tools and generative AI?'

usyd-claim-3.text: The University of Sydney's current student guidance (last updated 2 June 2026) says students can use AI in open (unsupervised) assessments, where educators guide the appropriate types of use and AI use must be acknowledged, but generally cannot use AI in secure (supervised) assessments unless the unit coordinator has given express permission in the unit outline. Each unit outline has a 'Use of AI' column showing, per assessment, AI prohibited, AI allowed, AI limited, or not applicable. This replaces the earlier Semester 1 2025 transition wording.

evidence.quote: Your unit outline includes a "Use of AI" column to indicate whether you can use AI or not for each assessment.
evidence.location: Unit of study outlines; lines 39-39 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You can use AI in open (unsupervised) assessments. These assessments support the development of disciplinary knowledge, as well as AI literacy. As such, you're encouraged to use AI tools productively and responsibly as part of your learning experience.
evidence.location: Allowed use; lines 55-55 of captured page text

evidence.quote: When you submit an open assessment, you'll need to appropriately acknowledge AI use so as not to breach academic integrity.
evidence.location: Allowed use; lines 59-59 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You generally can't use AI in secure (supervised) assessments, unless the unit coordinator has given express permission in the unit outline. Using AI when not allowed could amount to a breach of academic integrity, for which you could be investigated.
evidence.location: Prohibited use; lines 65-65 of captured page text

usyd-claim-4.text: The University of Sydney has adopted a 'two-lane approach' to assessment: Lane 1 comprises secure, in-person supervised assessments to assure learning, and Lane 2 comprises open assessments that support and scaffold the use of all available and relevant tools including generative AI.

evidence.quote: Secure (Lane 1) Open (Lane 2) Role of assessment Assessment of learning Assessment for and as learning Level of operation Mainly at program level Mainly at unit level Assessment security Secured, in person 'Open' / unsecured Role of generative AI May or may not be allowed by examiner As relevant, use of AI scaffolded & supported
evidence.location: The two-lane approach to assessment section, Table 1 summary

usyd-claim-5.text: The University of Sydney's generative AI guardrails state that confidential, personal, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information should not be entered into AI tools.

evidence.quote: Do not enter confidential, personal, proprietary or otherwise sensitive information Do not rely on the accuracy of outputs Openly acknowledge your use of AI (e.g. educators must model best practice by being transparent and clear with students about how these tools are used)
evidence.location: The policy and assessment frameworks section, 'The University of Sydney's guardrails around generative AI'

usyd-claim-6.text: The University of Sydney describes Microsoft Copilot Chat as the go-to option for students' AI needs: secure, supported and ready to use with public and protected information (but only some highly protected data), with students told always to sign in with their University account via Okta for data protection.

evidence.quote:
The go-to option for students' AI needs. Microsoft Copilot Chat is secure, supported, and ready to use with public and protected information (but only some highly protected data).
For data protection, always sign in with your University account via Okta.
evidence.location: AI tools you can use: Microsoft Copilot; lines 161-163 of captured page text

usyd-claim-7.text: University of Sydney guidance states that misusing AI can breach the Academic Integrity Policy, with examples including submitting AI-generated work without appropriate acknowledgment, using AI where it has been prohibited in a secure assessment such as a secure exam, and inputting University teaching or course materials, other students' content, external partners' intellectual property or any person's personal or health information. Citing non-existent references because AI output was not verified is not acceptable and risks an academic integrity breach.

evidence.quote:
Misusing AI can breach the Academic Integrity Policy. Examples of misuse include:
Submitting AI-generated work without appropriate acknowledgment
using AI where it has been prohibited in a ‘secure’ assessment type, such as during a secure exam
inputting University teaching or course materials, content generated by another student, intellectual property from external partners, or any person’s personal or health information.
evidence.location: Misuse of AI; lines 71-77 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Citing references that do not exist because you failed to verify AI outputs is not acceptable and puts you at risk of an academic integrity breach, alongside the likely loss of marks.
evidence.location: Misuse of AI (callout); lines 81-81 of captured page text

usyd-claim-8.text: If University of Sydney students use AI in assessments they must acknowledge it, including generative AI translation, paraphrasing or referencing tools; tools used only for word processing or basic spelling and grammar correction need not be acknowledged. Where permitted by the unit outline, the statement must say that AI tools were used and give the tool's name and version, the publisher, the URL and a brief description of how it was used; unit coordinators may add requirements such as a log of AI inputs and outputs.

evidence.quote: If you use AI in your assessments, you're required to acknowledge it – this includes acknowledging any tools that use generative AI, such as translation tools, paraphrasing tools or referencing tools. You are not required to acknowledge tools used for word processing, or which only correct basic spelling and grammar.
evidence.location: Acknowledging AI use; lines 89-89 of captured page text

evidence.quote:
If you're permitted to use automated writing tools or generative AI as per the unit outline, you will need to include a statement in your submitted work explaining:
that you have used AI tools in completing the work
the name and version of the automated writing or generative AI tools you have used
the publisher
the uniform resource locator (URL)
and a brief description of how you have used them.
evidence.location: What you need to provide; lines 95-105 of captured page text

evidence.quote: If your unit coordinator has made any additional stipulations about how they want the class to acknowledge AI use, you should also follow these rules. For example, they may require you to submit a log of the AI inputs and outputs used during the preparation of your assessment.
evidence.location: What you need to provide; lines 107-107 of captured page text

usyd-claim-9.text: The University of Sydney advises that Turnitin's AI detection tool may be used if a marker suspects AI-generated work where its use was not permitted or not acknowledged, but the AI detector score would not be the only evidence relied upon for an academic integrity case.

evidence.quote: If a marker or teacher suspects that part or all of your assessment has been generated using AI technology and its use was not permitted, or use was not acknowledged, the Turnitin AI detection tool may be used to evaluate the situation. It's important to note that the AI detector score would not be the only evidence relied upon for an academic integrity case, but will be considered alongside other relevant evidence.
evidence.location: Detecting generative AI use section

scope.en: McGill Code of Student Conduct and Disciplinary Procedures (Nov 2025); Principles on Generative AI in Teaching and Learning; Teaching and Academic Programs guidance; Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies research and thesis guidelines; IT Services AI guidance and governance; Linguistic Services translation guide. The 'AI Tools at McGill' directory requires login and was not re-verified. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 麦吉尔《学生行为与纪律程序守则》（2025 年 11 月）；生成式 AI 教学原则；教学与学术项目指引；研究生与博士后研究院（GPS）研究和论文指引；IT 服务 AI 指引与治理；语言服务翻译指南。“AI Tools at McGill”目录需登录，未能重新核实。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: There is no default university-wide permission or ban. Under the Code (Article 25(b)), students may not use generative AI in an assessment in a way not authorized by the instructor or supervisor or that breaks the course's AI requirements, and using a tool disallowed in the course outline or written instructions is cheating (Article 26(f)). Instructors are expected to state AI rules in their course outlines.
coursework.zh: 麦吉尔没有默认的全校许可或禁令。根据守则第 25(b) 条，学生不得以未经教师或导师授权、或违反课程 AI 要求的方式在考核中使用生成式 AI；使用课程大纲或书面说明禁止的工具属于作弊（第 26(f) 条）。教师应在课程大纲中写明 AI 规则。
coursework.meaningEn: Code Articles 25(b) and 26(f); course outline statements.
coursework.meaningZh: 守则第 25(b)、26(f) 条；课程大纲声明。

exams.en: Exams and other assessments follow the same Code rules: AI use not authorized by the instructor, or use of any tool disallowed in the course outline or assessment instructions, is an offence. No general exam permission exists.
exams.zh: 考试及其他考核适用同样的守则规定：未经教师授权使用 AI，或使用课程大纲或考核说明中禁止的工具，均属违规。不存在一般性的考试许可。
exams.meaningEn: Assessment-level authorization under the Code.
exams.meaningZh: 守则下的考核级授权。

disclosure.en: Students are responsible for verifying AI output and acknowledging AI use where applicable, following each instructor's explicit expectations. For master's and doctoral theses, GPS recommends (not yet requires) a GenAI statement and disclosure framework from 1 May 2026; non-disclosure may delay thesis assessment, and the framework may become mandatory after Fall 2026 consultations.
disclosure.zh: 学生须核实 AI 输出，并在适用时按各教师的明确要求注明 AI 使用。对于硕士和博士论文，GPS 自 2026 年 5 月 1 日起建议（尚非强制）加入生成式 AI 声明和披露框架；未披露可能延误论文评审，2026 年秋季咨询后可能改为强制。
disclosure.meaningEn: Fifth principle and GPS thesis guidelines.
disclosure.meaningZh: 第五原则与 GPS 论文指引。

privacy_data.en: Remove personally identifying information before using AI tools and do not use sensitive, PHI or PCI data. Even in McGill's secure Copilot version, users must not share private, sensitive, personal health, payment card or other confidential information.
privacy_data.zh: 使用 AI 工具前须去除可识别个人身份的信息，不得使用敏感、个人健康（PHI）或支付卡（PCI）数据。即使在麦吉尔的安全版 Copilot 中，也不得分享隐私、敏感、健康、支付卡或其他机密信息。
privacy_data.meaningEn: IT Services data guidance.
privacy_data.meaningZh: IT 服务数据指引。

approved_tools.en: McGill offers a secure (Commercial Data Protection) version of Microsoft Copilot with McGill credentials; the public version must not be used for McGill-related purposes. Unless formally reviewed and approved by McGill, generative AI tools may not be used for McGill-related purposes. For translating McGill content, DeepL Pro (paid) and enterprise Copilot are approved; free versions are prohibited. The full 'AI Tools at McGill' list could not be re-read (login required).
approved_tools.zh: 麦吉尔提供使用学校账号登录的安全版（商业数据保护）Microsoft Copilot；公共版不得用于与麦吉尔相关的工作。未经学校正式审查批准，不得将生成式 AI 工具用于麦吉尔相关用途。翻译麦吉尔内容时，可使用 DeepL Pro（付费版）和企业版 Copilot；免费版本被禁止。“AI Tools at McGill”完整列表需登录，未能重新读取。
approved_tools.meaningEn: IT Services tool guidance; directory login-restricted.
approved_tools.meaningZh: IT 服务工具指引；目录需登录。

research_publication.en: GPS research guidelines (November 2024) classify graduate AI uses as low-to-moderate risk (proofreading, light editing, debugging), moderate-to-high risk (content for one's own use) and very high risk (presenting AI-generated content as one's own, which is plagiarism under the Code). These are research guidelines, not course rules.
research_publication.zh: GPS 研究指引（2024 年 11 月）将研究生 AI 使用分为低至中等风险（校对、轻度编辑、调试代码）、中至高风险（为个人用途生成内容）和极高风险（把 AI 生成内容当作自己的成果，按守则属于剽窃）。这些是研究指引，不是课程规则。
research_publication.meaningEn: GPS research guidelines and thesis disclosure framework.
research_publication.meaningZh: GPS 研究指引与论文披露框架。

academic_integrity.en: AI-detection output alone cannot substantiate an Article 25 allegation, and McGill does not support relying on detectors. The University must prove an allegation on a balance of probabilities; students may have an Advisor at any interview or hearing. A CSD Hearing Committee decision can be appealed by notifying the Appeal Committee within 10 working days of official notice, on limited grounds; this deadline is specific to that committee's decisions.
academic_integrity.zh: 仅凭 AI 检测结果不足以认定第 25 条违规，麦吉尔也不支持依赖检测工具。学校须以“盖然性权衡”标准证明指控；学生在任何面谈或听证中都可以有顾问陪同。对学生纪律听证委员会（CSD）决定的上诉，须在收到正式通知后 10 个工作日内通知上诉委员会，且仅限特定理由；该期限仅适用于该委员会的决定。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Code evidence standard, Advisor right and Article 92 appeal.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 守则证据标准、顾问权利与第 92 条上诉。

do.en: Check the course outline and written assessment instructions for what AI use is authorized before using it.
do.zh: 使用 AI 前，查看课程大纲和书面考核说明中授权的使用范围。

do.en: Verify AI output and acknowledge AI use where applicable; thesis students should consider the GPS GenAI statement (recommended from 1 May 2026).
do.zh: 核实 AI 输出，并在适用时注明 AI 使用；论文学生应考虑使用 GPS 生成式 AI 声明（2026 年 5 月 1 日起建议采用）。

do.en: Use McGill's secure Copilot (McGill login) for McGill-related work, and bring an Advisor to any disciplinary interview if you wish.
do.zh: 处理麦吉尔相关工作时使用学校账号登录的安全版 Copilot；如有需要，可在纪律面谈中由顾问陪同。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI or any other tool that your course outline or assessment instructions disallow.
dont.zh: 不要使用课程大纲或考核说明禁止的生成式 AI 或其他工具。

dont.zh: 不要把个人、健康、支付卡或机密数据输入 AI 工具，也不要将未经审查的工具或免费公共版本用于麦吉尔相关用途。

cl-mcgill-university-microsoft-copilot-1.text: McGill IT Services' June 2024 article describes the secure Commercial Data Protection version of Microsoft Copilot, accessed via Microsoft Edge, as having undergone a data security and risk assessment and as the version McGill chose for McGill-related work. 'Commercial Data Protection' is the product name used in that 2024 article; the current Microsoft product name and McGill directory entry were not re-verified because the directory returned HTTP 403.

evidence.quote: McGill offers a secure version of Microsoft Copilot that protects our data, known as the Commercial Data Protection version. Microsoft Copilot is a powerful generative AI tool where an AI chatbot can help answer questions, generate content, and more! Microsoft Copilot can be accessed via Microsoft Edge.

scope.en: Université PSL Règlement de la scolarité 2026-2027 (Board, 25 June 2026; applies to programmes PSL operates directly); PSL Charte du doctorat (June 2026); CIENS (ENS-PSL) AI charter; Dauphine-PSL library research-integrity guidance. Member institutions keep their own rules. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 巴黎文理研究大学（PSL）2026–2027《学业规则》（2026 年 6 月 25 日董事会通过，适用于 PSL 直接运营的项目）；PSL《博士章程》（2026 年 6 月）；高师 CIENS 中心 AI 章程；巴黎九大图书馆科研诚信指引。各成员机构保留自身规则。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: In programmes PSL operates directly, AI tools may be used only where the instructor authorises them, and their use must then be disclosed. Member institutions (ENS, Dauphine, Mines Paris and others) apply their own regulations; for example the CIENS centre at ENS-PSL allows AI only as occasional help (translation, document exploration, organising work) and bans AI-written text content.
coursework.zh: 在 PSL 直接运营的项目中，只有在教师授权时才可使用 AI 工具，且使用后必须披露。成员机构（高师、巴黎九大、巴黎矿业等）适用各自规则；例如高师 CIENS 中心只允许把 AI 作为临时辅助（翻译、文献探索、安排工作），并禁止用 AI 撰写正文。
coursework.meaningEn: Instructor authorisation under the 2026-27 regulation; member-institution rules.
coursework.meaningZh: 2026–27 学业规则下的教师授权；成员机构规则。

exams.en: The reviewed PSL sources do not set a general AI rule for examinations beyond anti-fraud measures; follow each programme's exam rules and instructor authorisation. This is an evidence gap, not a permission.
exams.zh: 所审核的 PSL 来源除防作弊措施外，没有设定针对考试的一般 AI 规则；请遵守各项目的考试规定和教师授权。这是证据缺口，并非许可。
exams.meaningEn: No general exam AI rule found in reviewed sources.
exams.meaningZh: 所审核来源中未发现一般考试 AI 规则。

disclosure.en: Where an instructor authorises AI, its use must be disclosed explicitly like any source citation; undisclosed use is treated as plagiarism. Doctoral candidates must include a signed 'Déclaration doctorale d'intégrité scientifique' listing AI tools, tasks, benefits, limits and risks. CIENS requires AI use to be noted in a note or the text.
disclosure.zh: 教师授权使用 AI 时，须像引用任何来源一样明确披露；未披露的使用按剽窃处理。博士生须在论文中附签署的《博士科研诚信声明》，列明所用 AI 工具、任务、优缺点和风险。CIENS 要求在注释或正文中注明 AI 使用情况。
disclosure.meaningEn: Article 3 disclosure; doctoral declaration; CIENS transparency.
disclosure.meaningZh: 第 3 条披露；博士声明；CIENS 透明要求。

privacy_data.en: CIENS prohibits giving AI sensitive, protected or confidential information. Dauphine-PSL library guidance advises not sharing personal data with third parties and checking that generated text contains no personal data. No PSL-wide AI data rule was found in the reviewed sources.
privacy_data.zh: CIENS 禁止向 AI 提供敏感、受保护或机密信息。巴黎九大图书馆指引建议不要与第三方共享个人数据，并检查生成文本不含个人数据。所审核来源中未发现全 PSL 统一的 AI 数据规则。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Unit and library guidance on data.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 机构与图书馆数据指引。

approved_tools.en: No PSL-wide list of approved or licensed AI tools was found in the reviewed sources. ChatGPT is mentioned only as an example of an AI tool, not as a required or provided service.
approved_tools.zh: 所审核来源中未发现全 PSL 统一的获批或授权 AI 工具清单。ChatGPT 只是作为 AI 工具示例被提及，不是要求使用或学校提供的服务。
approved_tools.meaningEn: No institutional tool list found.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 未发现机构工具清单。

research_publication.en: Generative AI is not prohibited in PSL doctoral research, but uses must be transparent, declared and critically assessed; the candidate remains fully responsible and member institutions may set stricter rules. Dauphine-PSL library guidance recommends stating the tool, version and context, not treating AI as a co-author, and notes reproducibility risks; these are recommendations at a member institution.
research_publication.zh: PSL 博士研究不禁止使用生成式 AI，但使用必须透明、声明并接受批判性审视；博士生承担全部责任，成员机构可设更严格规则。巴黎九大图书馆指引建议注明工具、版本和使用背景，不将 AI 视为合著者，并提示可重复性风险；这些属于成员机构的建议。
research_publication.meaningEn: Doctoral charter 2.7 and library guidance.
research_publication.meaningZh: 博士章程 2.7 节与图书馆指引。

academic_integrity.en: Failure to disclose AI use is treated and sanctioned as plagiarism. On suspicion, the instructor informs the programme management and a disciplinary procedure may follow, with sanctions up to exclusion (not automatic). At CIENS, undeclared AI use may be treated as academic fraud.
academic_integrity.zh: 未披露 AI 使用按剽窃认定和处罚。出现怀疑时，教师须告知项目管理团队，可能启动纪律程序，处分最高可至开除（并非自动）。在 CIENS，未声明的 AI 使用可能被视为学术欺诈。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Article 3 plagiarism procedure.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 第 3 条剽窃程序。

draft-claim-psl-ciens-ai-charter.text: The AI charter of CIENS (an interdisciplinary centre of ENS-PSL) applies to CIENS students, teachers and researchers only. It allows generative AI as occasional help for translation, document exploration, exploratory document analysis or organising work, but prohibits producing false references, developing a research problem and scientific reasoning, writing the text content, and giving AI sensitive, protected or confidential information. Any AI use must be stated in a note or the body of the text, naming the tool and the nature of use; undeclared use may be treated as academic fraud and lead to disciplinary sanctions. These are unit-level rules, not PSL-wide rules.

draft-claim-psl-doctoral-charter-genai.text: PSL's Charte du doctorat (June 2026, section 2.7) sets general recommendations on generative AI for doctoral candidates, some of which are mandatory. Generative AI is not prohibited in doctoral research, but its uses must be transparent, declared and critically assessed, and the candidate remains fully responsible for AI-obtained content. Candidates must insert a dated, signed 'Déclaration doctorale d'intégrité scientifique' (one to two pages) at the start of the thesis, stating which generative AI tools were used, for which tasks, their benefits, limits and risks, and any mitigation. Member institutions may set stricter rules, which prevail.

The 2026 version applies to programmes operated directly by PSL (such as the Collège Sciences, Humanités et Société and the Paris School of AI); member institutions apply their own regulations, so it does not set course permissions across ENS, Dauphine, Mines Paris and other members.

Ne pas signaler l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle est considéré comme un acte de plagiat et sera sanctionné comme tel.

Dans le cadre des réponses obtenues, il faut vérifier que le texte généré ne constitue pas un plagiat ou ne contient pas de données personnelles.

psl-claim-research-limitations.text: The Dauphine-PSL library's guidance notes that generative AI undermines research reproducibility, a basic principle of scientific integrity, because models' code and algorithms may be unknown and change regularly. This is a risk statement, not a prohibition on AI use.

scope.en: University of Toronto Code of Behaviour on Academic Matters (effective July 1, 2025); Vice-Provost Teaching & Learning generative AI FAQ (October 2026); School of Graduate Studies AI guidance (September 2026); CTSI and AI Kitchen tool information; Information Security guidelines; UTSC CTL tool list. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 多伦多大学《学术事务行为守则》（2025 年 7 月 1 日生效）；教学副教务长办公室生成式 AI 常见问题（2026 年 10 月）；研究生院 AI 指引（2026 年 9 月）；CTSI 与 AI Kitchen 工具信息；信息安全指引；士嘉堡校区教学中心工具列表。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: Marked work: if an instructor says no outside assistance is permitted, using generative AI is typically treated as an unauthorized aid under the Code; instructors are asked to state their rules in the syllabus. Separately, students may generally use AI as a learning aid (to summarize or test understanding) even when a course bans AI for assignments, and such study use usually need not be disclosed.
coursework.zh: 计分作业：如果教师规定不得借助外部帮助，使用生成式 AI 通常会被视为守则下的“未经授权辅助工具”；学校要求教师在课程大纲中写明规则。另外，即使课程禁止在作业中使用 AI，学生一般仍可把 AI 作为学习辅助（总结信息、检验理解），这类学习用途通常无需披露。
coursework.meaningEn: Unauthorized-aid rule for marked work vs. learning-aid use.
coursework.meaningZh: 计分作业的未授权辅助规则与学习辅助用途的区分。

exams.en: Using or possessing an unauthorized aid in any academic work, including tests and exams, is an offence under the 2025 Code. No general exam permission for AI exists; follow each assessment's instructions.
exams.zh: 根据 2025 年守则，在任何学术作业（包括测验和考试）中使用或持有未经授权的辅助工具均属违规。不存在一般性的考试 AI 许可；请遵守各项考核说明。
exams.meaningEn: Code s.4(b).
exams.meaningZh: 守则第 4(b) 条。

disclosure.en: Learning-aid use typically does not need to be cited or disclosed, but if you use AI-generated information that would normally need citation (quoting, paraphrasing, reproducing ideas), cite it per U of T Libraries guidance or your instructor. Doctoral theses must clearly describe and cite any approved AI use (which tools, how and why).
disclosure.zh: 学习辅助用途通常无需引用或披露；但如果使用了通常需要引用的 AI 生成信息（引述、改写、复述观点），须按多大图书馆指引或教师要求引用。博士论文必须清楚描述并引用任何获批的 AI 使用（哪些工具、如何及为何使用）。
disclosure.meaningEn: Citation rule and doctoral thesis description.
disclosure.meaningZh: 引用规则与博士论文说明要求。

privacy_data.en: Before sharing personal information or Level 2-4 university data with any AI tool, verify it has been assessed for that level; AI Kitchen tools are approved up to Level 3 (the Model Comparison Tool only to Level 2). Without the instructor's explicit permission, students may not upload course materials (slides, recordings, test questions, rubrics) to an AI tool not approved for that purpose. Instructors using unvetted third-party AI tools must let students opt out with a viable alternative, and a Privacy Impact Assessment is required when personal information is collected.
privacy_data.zh: 在向任何 AI 工具分享个人信息或 2–4 级大学数据之前，须确认该工具已通过相应等级评估；AI Kitchen 工具获批至 3 级（模型比较工具仅至 2 级）。未经教师明确许可，学生不得把课程材料（课件、录像、试题、评分标准）上传到未获批的 AI 工具。教师使用未经审查的第三方 AI 工具时，必须允许学生退出并提供可行替代方案；收集个人信息时须做隐私影响评估（PIA）。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Data levels, course-materials rule and third-party tool safeguards.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 数据等级、课程材料规则与第三方工具保障。

approved_tools.en: Students can use Microsoft Copilot Chat (free, U of T login) and Cogniti agents that instructors enable in Quercus. Claude for Education (free, limited seats), ChatGPT Edu (negotiated pricing, limited seats), M365 Copilot, Teams Premium, GitHub Copilot Business and Azure AI Foundry are for staff, faculty and librarians. Three U of T-built AIK services are Coming Soon. Library features such as Scopus AI and Web of Science Research Assistant, and Contact North tools, are listed by UTSC. Access does not authorize use in an assessment.
approved_tools.zh: 学生可使用 Microsoft Copilot Chat（免费，多大账号登录）及教师在 Quercus 课程中启用的 Cogniti 智能体。Claude for Education（免费、名额有限）、ChatGPT Edu（议价、名额有限）、M365 Copilot、Teams Premium、GitHub Copilot Business 和 Azure AI Foundry 面向员工、教师和图书馆员。三项多大自建 AIK 服务尚为“即将推出”。Scopus AI、Web of Science Research Assistant 等图书馆功能及 Contact North 工具由士嘉堡校区列出。能使用工具不代表获准在考核中使用。
approved_tools.meaningEn: AI Kitchen directory, CTSI and UTSC listings.
approved_tools.meaningZh: AI Kitchen 目录、CTSI 与士嘉堡校区列表。

research_publication.en: Any AI use in researching or writing a doctoral thesis requires prior approval from the supervisor(s) and supervisory committee, and approval for research does not cover writing. For other graduate milestones SGS recommends documented advance approval; master's theses, MRPs and comprehensive exams are governed by graduate units. Unauthorized AI use may be an academic offence or research misconduct.
research_publication.zh: 博士论文研究或写作中的任何 AI 使用都须事先获得导师和指导委员会批准，研究方面的批准不涵盖写作。对其他研究生学业节点，研究生院建议事先取得书面批准；硕士论文、主要研究论文（MRP）和综合考试由各研究生单位规定。未经授权的 AI 使用可能构成学术违规或科研不端。
research_publication.meaningEn: SGS doctoral (required) vs. general milestone (recommended) rules.
research_publication.meaningZh: 研究生院博士论文（强制）与一般学业节点（建议）规则。

academic_integrity.en: The 2025 Code also covers knowingly submitting concocted facts or references. An instructor with reasonable grounds must tell the student and invite a discussion (what the student says there cannot be used at a hearing); at the dean's meeting students may seek advice or representation and are not obliged to make statements. Divisional sanctions go up to 12 months' suspension (24 with Provost approval); longer suspension or a recommendation of expulsion is for the University Tribunal. U of T does not support AI-detection software on student work.
academic_integrity.zh: 2025 年守则也涵盖明知而提交捏造的事实或参考文献。教师有合理理由时须告知学生并邀请面谈（面谈中所说内容不得在听证中作为证据）；在院长面谈时，学生可寻求建议或代理，且无义务作出陈述。院系可施加最长 12 个月停学（经教务长批准可至 24 个月）；更长停学或建议开除由大学法庭决定。多大不支持对学生作业使用 AI 检测软件。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Code offences, divisional procedure, sanctions and detector position.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 守则违规、院系程序、处分与检测立场。

do.zh: 使用 AI 生成的措辞、观点或信息时，按多大图书馆指引或教师要求引用。

dont.zh: 不要把个人信息或 2–4 级数据分享给未经相应等级评估的 AI 工具。

dont.en: Do not submit AI-generated facts or references without checking them; concocted references are an offence under the Code.
dont.zh: 不要未经核实就提交 AI 生成的事实或参考文献；捏造参考文献属于守则违规。

draft-claim-uoft-code-fabricated-referen.text: The 2025 Code of Behaviour on Academic Matters also makes it an offence knowingly to submit academic work containing a purported statement of fact or reference to a source that has been concocted (an offence depending on knowledge, including where the student ought reasonably to have known; not every AI error is automatically an offence). When an instructor has reasonable grounds to believe an offence was committed, they must inform the student immediately, give reasons and invite a discussion, normally held synchronously; nothing the student says in that discussion may be used in evidence at a hearing. The dean or chair must tell the student they may seek advice or be represented and are not obliged to make any statement. Sanctions available at divisional level include up to 12 months' suspension (up to 24 with Provost approval); suspension of up to five years or a recommendation of expulsion are for the University Tribunal.

Nothing the student says in such a discussion may be used or receivable in evidence against the student in the hearing of any charge with respect to the alleged offence in question.

draft-claim-uoft-learning-aid-use.text: The University of Toronto FAQ (updated October 2026) says undergraduate and graduate students may use generative AI tools as learning aids, for example to summarize information or test their understanding, in a manner similar to consulting books, peers or a tutor. Such uses are generally acceptable even if an instructor has said AI is not otherwise permitted in the course, and typically do not need to be cited or disclosed. If students use AI-generated information that would normally require citation (quoting, paraphrasing or reproducing text or ideas), they must cite it according to U of T Libraries guidance or the instructor's directions. Learning-aid use is distinct from using AI to complete marked work.

These tools should be used in a manner similar to consulting library books, online sources, peers, or a tutor. draft-claim-uoft-third-party-tools-pia.text: University of Toronto CTSI guidance on using non-supported (unvetted) AI tools in courses says students must be able to opt out: instructors cannot require students to accept a third party's terms or hand over personal data or intellectual property, and must provide a viable alternative where the tool is part of a required activity or assessment. A Privacy Impact Assessment is required wherever an unvetted tool collects personally identifying information, typically taking four to eight weeks.

evidence.quote: Students must be able to opt out. You cannot require students to accept a third party’s terms or hand over personal data or intellectual property. If the tool is part of a required activity or assessment, you must provide a viable alternative for students who decline.

Under U of T’s FIPPA obligations, any unvetted tool that collects personal information (e.g., student names, email addresses, assessment submissions) needs a PIA to be conducted. This process typically takes four to eight weeks from the time all required information has been received.

uoft-claim-academic-integrity.text: Under the University of Toronto Code of Behaviour on Academic Matters (effective July 1, 2025), it is an offence for a student knowingly to use or possess an unauthorized aid or obtain unauthorized assistance in connection with any form of academic work. If an instructor has specified that no outside assistance is permitted on an assignment, the University would typically consider the student's use of generative AI to be use of an unauthorized aid. The Office of Academic Integrity scenario page gives the same example but still shows pre-2025 Code wording and is interpretive rather than the governing text.

evidence.quote: to use or possess an unauthorized aid or aids or obtain or provide unauthorized assistance in connection with any form of academic work;
evidence.location: Code s.4(b) (Offences); lines 565-565 of captured page text

evidence.quote: if an instructor specified that no outside assistance was permitted on an assignment, the University would typically consider a student’s use of generative AI to be use of an “unauthorized aid” under the Code of Behaviour on Academic Matters.
evidence.location: What is the University's position on students' use of AI on assignments? (updated October 2026); lines 224-224 of captured page text

evidence.quote: If your instructor advised you that use of AI tools was prohibited, using a generative AI tool to create even part of your marked assignment would be considered use of an unauthorized aid.
evidence.location: Scenario (interpretive; pre-2025 Code numbering); lines 51-51 of captured page text

uoft-claim-approved-tools.text: University of Toronto teaching guidance (CTSI) now names Cogniti as the preferred tool for teaching and learning, embedded in Quercus and free for every student, and Microsoft Copilot Chat as the easiest general-purpose starting point available to everyone at U of T. Tools in the AI Kitchen are vetted and may be used with institutional data up to Level 3. Some licensed tools require a paid subscription not covered by the University. Tool availability does not authorize AI use in a given assessment.

evidence.quote: Cogniti is the preferred tool for teaching and learning. It is built for education: embedded in Quercus, free for every student, highly customizable, and can be grounded in your course content.
evidence.location: GenAI Tools for Teaching: overview; lines 73-73 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Microsoft Copilot Chat is the easiest place to start. It is a general-purpose tool available to everyone at U of T and is the lowest-barrier way for students to build basic AI literacy.
evidence.location: GenAI Tools for Teaching: overview; lines 75-75 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Licensed Tools in the AI Kitchen (such as Claude for Education, ChatGPT Edu and M365 Copilot) may suit your own course preparation and other projects where advanced features can add value. However, some of these tools require a paid subscription that is not covered by the University.
evidence.location: GenAI Tools for Teaching: overview; lines 77-77 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Tools in the AI Kitchen are vetted for privacy and security and covered by U of T’s data protection standards: your prompts and your students’ data are never used to train AI models, and you can use institutional data up to Level 3, such as course materials and student assessments.
evidence.location: GenAI Tools for Teaching: overview; lines 69-69 of captured page text

uoft-claim-graduate-supervisor-approval.text: For graduate academic milestones generally (for example comprehensive exams, candidacy and other scholarly activities), the University of Toronto School of Graduate Studies recommends that students seek and document in writing unambiguous approval from their supervisor(s) and supervisory committee before using generative AI. This general recommendation sits alongside stricter mandatory rules for the doctoral thesis (see claim-university-of-toronto-001); students, supervisors and graduate units must agree in advance how any AI tools will be used for each milestone.

evidence.quote: It is recommended that students seek and document in writing unambiguous approval from their supervisor(s) and supervisory committee in advance of the use of generative AI tools in research, writing, or other scholarly activities relevant to graduate academic milestones.
evidence.location: Overview (last updated September 9, 2026); lines 45-45 of captured page text

evidence.quote: This includes transparency between students, their supervisors, and graduate units, who must agree in advance how any generative AI tools will be used in the context of each academic milestone;
evidence.location: Overview; lines 43-43 of captured page text

uoft-claim-privacy-data.text: University of Toronto Information Security guidelines state that no data should be provided to generative AI if any part of it should not appear in that system's results, and that before sharing personal information or university data classified as Level 2, 3 or 4 with any AI tool, users must verify the tool has been assessed by the university as suitable for that data type and level. AI Kitchen tools are approved for Level 3 data or below, except the Model Comparison Tool, which is approved only up to Level 2.

evidence.quote: No data should be provided to generative AI if any part of that data should not be included in results produced by that system.
evidence.location: Recognize privacy and information security risks; lines 201-201 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Before sharing personal information or university data classified as level 2, 3 or 4 with any AI tool, verify that the tool has been assessed by the university as suitable for that data type and classification level.
evidence.location: Recognize privacy and information security risks; lines 207-207 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Approved for Level 3 data (or below)*
evidence.location: AI Kitchen standards; lines 69-69 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Approved only for data classified up to and including Level 2.
evidence.location: AIK Model Comparison Tool row; lines 89-89 of captured page text

uoft-claim-syllabus-statement.text: The University of Toronto recommends that instructors include a syllabus statement informing students of their expectations on AI use, and provides sample statements for syllabi and assignments for graduate and undergraduate courses; some units may have their own guidelines. The earlier Vice-Provost URL now redirects to the office home page, so the current Vice-Provost, Teaching & Learning FAQ (updated October 2026) is used as the source.

evidence.quote: The University recommends that you include a statement on your syllabus that informs students about your expectations with respect to the use of AI. We have created sample statements for instructors to include in course syllabi and course assignments to help shape the message to students about what AI technology is, or is not, allowed. These statements may be used for both graduate and undergraduate level courses. Note: Some units and divisions may have also developed guidelines for their instructors.
evidence.location: Sample syllabus statements (last updated October 2026); lines 68-68 of captured page text

scope.en: Fudan rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (24 Sep 2024, trial; reproduced in a college's 2024 thesis rules); Fudan official news on the Generative AI Teaching Application Guide 1.0 (Jan 2026; guide text itself not reviewed); Student Disciplinary and Student Appeals Regulations; Information Office AI Service Hall notice. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 《复旦大学关于在本科毕业论文（设计）中使用 AI 工具的规定（试行）》（2024 年 9 月 24 日；见某学院 2024 年论文管理办法附件）；复旦官方关于《生成式人工智能教育教学应用指引 1.0 版》的报道（2026 年 1 月；指引全文未审核）；学生纪律处分条例与学生申诉处理条例；信息办 AI 办事大厅公告。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: No blanket ban on AI in ordinary courses was found. According to Fudan's official announcement, the January 2026 teaching guide allows AI for supporting steps such as language polishing and structural suggestions but not for core academic work, and expects course syllabi to set AI conditions. The stricter undergraduate-thesis rule applies to course, term and exam papers only where no specific rule exists ('may refer to').
coursework.zh: 未发现普通课程全面禁止 AI 的规定。据复旦官方报道，2026 年 1 月的教学应用指引允许在语言润色、结构建议等辅助环节使用 AI，但不得替代核心学术劳动，并要求课程大纲明确 AI 使用条件。更严格的本科毕业论文规定仅在“无具体针对性规定”时可供课程论文、学年论文和考试论文“参照执行”。
coursework.meaningEn: Course-level rules; 2026 teaching guide as reported.
coursework.meaningZh: 课程层面规则；2026 年指引（据官方报道）。

exams.en: No general exam AI rule was found; exam papers may refer to the undergraduate-thesis rule where no specific rule exists. Follow each course and exam's instructions.
exams.zh: 未发现一般性的考试 AI 规则；在无具体规定时，考试论文可参照本科毕业论文规定执行。请遵守各课程和考试的说明。
exams.meaningEn: Exam use not set university-wide.
exams.meaningZh: 考试使用未有全校统一规定。

disclosure.en: For undergraduate theses, any AI use must be disclosed in the thesis commitment form: tool name and version, time and purpose, what the AI produced, where it was used, plus keeping pre-AI materials for inspection. The 2026 teaching guide, as reported, judges integrity mainly on honest disclosure and process records.
disclosure.zh: 本科毕业论文中使用 AI，必须在承诺书中披露：工具名称和版本、使用时间与用途、AI 生成的内容或建议、在论文中的使用部分，并保留 AI 处理前的重要材料以备检查。据报道，2026 年教学指引主要依据是否如实披露和有无过程记录判断学术诚信。
disclosure.meaningEn: Thesis rule Art. 5; teaching guide as reported.
disclosure.meaningZh: 论文规定第五条；教学指引（据报道）。

privacy_data.en: Undergraduate theses involving confidential content may not use any AI tool or upload any data or images to AI platforms. No broader university AI data rule was found in the reviewed sources; the AI Service Hall states it uses a locally deployed model to protect data (not independently verified).
privacy_data.zh: 涉及保密内容的本科毕业论文禁止使用任何 AI 工具，禁止向 AI 平台上传任何数据和图片。所审核来源中未发现更广泛的全校 AI 数据规则；AI 办事大厅称采用本地化部署模型保护数据（未经独立核实）。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Thesis rule Art. 4(6).
privacy_data.meaningZh: 论文规定第四条第 6 项。

approved_tools.en: Fudan's AI Service Hall (eHall, March 2025) provides administrative services through modules 复小搜 (search) and 复小填 (form filling, three initial service items); 复小信 is an earlier Q&A assistant from 2021. The AI3A platform (January 2026) gathers teaching cases and course-level tools. These are not a list of tools approved for coursework.
approved_tools.zh: 复旦 AI 办事大厅（eHall，2025 年 3 月）通过“复小搜”（搜索）和“复小填”（填报，首批 3 个服务事项）模块提供行政服务；“复小信”是 2021 年上线的问答助手。AI³A 平台（2026 年 1 月）汇集教学案例和课程级工具。这些并非获准用于课程作业的工具清单。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Information Office notice and AI3A announcement.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 信息办公告与 AI³A 平台报道。

research_publication.en: The AI thesis rule covers undergraduate theses only and expressly excludes published papers and research activities, which are governed by other rules. Fudan's 2026 graduate thesis format norms contain no AI provision; graduate students should check their school, supervisor and the Graduate School for applicable rules.
research_publication.zh: AI 论文规定仅适用于本科毕业论文，并明确排除发表的学术论文和学术研究活动，后者另有规定。复旦 2026 年研究生学位论文规范（格式）中没有 AI 条款；研究生应向所在院系、导师和研究生院确认适用规则。
research_publication.meaningEn: Scope exclusion; no graduate AI rule found.
research_publication.meaningZh: 适用范围排除；未发现研究生 AI 规则。

academic_integrity.en: In undergraduate theses AI may only assist (with supervisor consent) with literature search, chart suggestions, non-innovative code and reference formatting, and is banned for research design, data, key figures, writing text, language polishing and translation. Breaches are handled by seriousness, from the thesis grade or barring the defence to discipline and degree consequences only where misconduct is found. Disciplinary decisions can be appealed to the University Student Appeals Committee within 10 days, then to the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission within 15 days.
academic_integrity.zh: 本科毕业论文中，AI 仅可在征得指导教师同意后辅助文献检索、图表类型推荐、非创新性代码和参考文献格式整理，禁止用于研究设计、数据、关键图表、正文撰写、语言润色和翻译。违规视情节处理，从计入论文成绩、不准答辩，到构成学术不端时才给予纪律处分和学位处理。纪律处分可在 10 日内向学校学生申诉处理委员会申诉，对复查决定不服可在 15 日内向上海市教委申诉。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Thesis rule Arts. 3, 4, 7 and appeal regulations.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 论文规定第三、四、七条与申诉条例。

do.en: Undergraduate thesis: get your supervisor's consent before any AI use, and only for literature search, chart-type suggestions, non-innovative code or reference formatting.
do.zh: 本科毕业论文：使用 AI 前须征得指导教师同意，且仅限文献检索、图表类型推荐、非创新性代码或参考文献格式整理。

do.en: Disclose AI tool, version, time, purpose, outputs and where it was used in the thesis commitment form, and keep pre-AI materials.
do.zh: 在承诺书中披露 AI 工具、版本、时间、用途、生成内容及使用位置，并保留 AI 处理前的材料。

do.en: For ordinary courses, follow the course syllabus AI terms; if disciplined, you may appeal within 10 days of service.
do.zh: 普通课程遵循课程大纲中的 AI 条款；如受纪律处分，可在送达之日起 10 日内申诉。

dont.en: Do not use AI to write, polish or translate undergraduate thesis text, or to design research or analyse data.
dont.zh: 不要用 AI 撰写、润色或翻译本科毕业论文正文，也不要用于研究设计或数据分析。

dont.en: Do not generate or alter original data or key result figures with AI.
dont.zh: 不要用 AI 生成或修改原始数据或关键结果图。

dont.en: Do not use any AI tool, or upload data or images, for a thesis involving confidential content.
dont.zh: 涉密论文不要使用任何 AI 工具，也不要上传任何数据或图片。

evidence.quote: 2025年3月14日，继2021年智能问答助手“复小信”上线后，信息办依托一站式低代码开发平台，深度融合AI智能填报引擎，智能推出AI办事大厅，实现平台级智能化支撑。

cl-fudan-university-institutional-ai-ser.text: 复小填 (intelligent form filling) is a module of Fudan's AI Service Hall (eHall); at launch in March 2025 its 'one-sentence service' covered three initial administrative service items. The 2025 initial scope is not evidence of its 2026 scope. It is an administrative service tool, not a coursework permission.
