evidence.location: AI办事大厅上线公告; lines 157-157 of captured page text

cl-fudan-university-self-deploy-197.text: Fudan's Information Office states that its AI Service Hall uses a locally deployed Tongyi Qianwen (Qwen) model to protect staff and student data. This is the University's own statement; the back-end architecture and data security were not independently verified.

evidence.quote: 复旦大学AI办事大厅采用通义千问本地化部署，全方位守护师生数据安全。
evidence.location: AI办事大厅上线公告; lines 159-159 of captured page text

draft-claim-fudan-2026-teaching-guide.text: On 12 January 2026 Fudan launched the AI3A education co-creation platform and published the Generative AI Education and Teaching Application Guide 1.0, with 11 annexes such as an AI use declaration template and reference syllabus clauses. According to Fudan's official announcement, the guide allows AI for supporting steps such as language polishing and structural suggestions but not to replace core academic work such as research conception, theory building and data analysis, and judges integrity mainly on honest disclosure and process records. The guide's full text sits on the AI3A platform and was not independently reviewed; it is teaching guidance and does not by itself override the stricter undergraduate-thesis rule.

evidence.quote: 1月12日，复旦大学正式上线AI3A教育共创平台，同步发布《复旦大学生成式人工智能教育教学应用指引1.0版》
evidence.location: 官方新闻（2026-01-13）; lines 291-291 of captured page text

evidence.quote: 它明确，AI可用于语言润色、结构建议等辅助环节，但不得替代研究构思、理论构建、数据分析等核心学术劳动。判定依据则侧重于学生是否如实披露、是否有过程记录可供核查，以及教师是否通过课程要求、答辩等方式进行了合理性验证。

evidence.quote: 而《应用指引》更是一个“拿来即用”的工具包，附有11个可操作的附件，涵盖教学设计模板、伦理声明范例、课堂协议等，真正让师生用好、用对AI。
evidence.location: 官方新闻; lines 295-295 of captured page text

draft-claim-fudan-discipline-appeal.text: Under Fudan's Student Disciplinary Regulations (2017, amended 2019), students must be informed of their right to state their case and defend themselves before a sanction. A student who disagrees with a disciplinary decision may appeal to the University Student Appeals Committee within ten days (not working days) of service of the decision; the committee normally concludes within fifteen days (extendable by fifteen), and a student who disagrees with the review decision may appeal to the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission within fifteen days of its service (Student Appeals Regulations, effective 1 September 2017). A teacher's request to redo or supplement an assessment is not automatically a disciplinary decision.

evidence.quote: 第十六条 学生本人不服处分决定的，可以在处分决定书送达之日起十日内向学校学生申诉处理委员会提出申诉。
evidence.location: 学生纪律处分条例 第十六条; physical PDF page 5; lines 200-202 of captured PDF text

evidence.quote: 学生提出申诉，应当在处理决定书送达之日起十日内，向学生申诉处理委员会递交申诉申请书，并提供处理决定书的副本。
evidence.location: 学生申诉处理条例 第十四条; lines 175-175 of captured page text

evidence.quote: 学生申诉处理委员会对申诉案件，应当在收到申诉申请书之日起十五日内作出复查结论并告知申诉人。有特殊情况需要延长的，由学生申诉处理委员会主任批准，可以延长十五日。
evidence.location: 第二十九条; lines 253-253 of captured page text

evidence.quote: 申诉人对复查决定有异议的，在复查决定书送达之日起十五日内，可以向上海市教育委员会提出申诉。

draft-claim-fudan-thesis-ai-consequences.text: Under the Fudan undergraduate-thesis AI rule, breaches are handled according to their seriousness: they may be reflected in the thesis assessment grade, lead to refusal of the defence or cancellation of a passing grade, and only where they constitute academic misconduct lead to disciplinary sanctions, loss of degree eligibility or degree revocation. Course papers, term papers and exam papers may refer to this rule where no specific rule exists, while published academic papers and research activities are governed by other rules and are outside its scope. Supervisors and reviewers may add supplementary assessment to check the student's mastery.

evidence.quote: 学生违反相关规定使用 AI 工具的，视情节给予纳入本科毕业论文（设计）考核成绩、不准答辩、取消合格成绩等处理；构成学术不端（不当）的，按照相关校纪校规给予纪律处分、取消学位申请资格、撤销学位等处理。

The author bears final responsibility and AI cannot be listed as an author.

draft-claim-fudan-thesis-ai-prohibitions.text: The same Fudan undergraduate-thesis rule (Article 4) prohibits AI in six areas: research design and data analysis; generating or altering original data (unless AI itself is the research topic); generating or altering original result images and key illustrations (unless a reproducible AI method is part of the design and explained in the methods); directly generating thesis text or acknowledgements, including AI language polishing and translation; use of AI by defence committee members or reviewers to evaluate the thesis; and any AI use or upload for theses involving confidential content.

evidence.quote: 研究设计与数据分析：禁止使用 AI 工具进行研究方案设计、创新性方法设计、算法（模型）框架搭建、毕业论文（设计）结构设计、研究（设计）选题、研究（设计）意义及创新性总结、研究假设提出、数据分析、结果分析与讨论和结论总结等。

evidence.quote: 语言表达能力仍然是毕业论文（设计）考察的重点，禁止使用 AI 工具进行语言润色和翻译。

fudan-claim-001.text: Fudan's formal rule on AI tools in undergraduate theses (adopted by the Academic Affairs Office on 24 September 2024, trial) allows AI use only with the supervisor's consent and only where AI output does not affect assessment of the student's own innovative ability, in four areas: literature search and management (verifying references), suggesting chart types and auxiliary charting (not generating or altering original data or key research figures), coding and method screening where the method is not the thesis's innovation (all code and methods must be reviewed and tested by the author), and reference formatting (with checking). This rule is specific to undergraduate theses; it is not a rule for all courses or for graduate theses.

scope.en: King's College London generative AI guidance (student, doctoral, AI-assisted marking, context, macro-level; last updated April/July 2025); Academic Misconduct Policy (effective 1 September 2023, status Current, next review September 2026). Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 伦敦国王学院生成式 AI 指引（学生、博士、AI 辅助评分、背景与定义、宏观层面；2025 年 4 月/7 月更新）；《学术不端政策》（2023 年 9 月 1 日生效，状态为现行，计划 2026 年 9 月复审）。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: King's does not ban AI, but the level allowed is set per assessment using four suggested levels: Minimal (spell/grammar checkers, transcription), Limited/selective (delineated tasks), Open (no specific restrictions but key stages tracked) and Embedded (AI is part of the task). Copying AI output into a submission is not appropriate under the Academic Misconduct Policy, and work must remain the student's own; ask if unsure.
coursework.zh: 国王学院不禁止 AI，但每项考核允许的程度由考核说明按四个建议等级设定：Minimal（拼写语法检查、自动转写）、Limited/selective（限定任务）、Open（无具体限制但须记录关键步骤）、Embedded（AI 是任务组成部分）。根据《学术不端政策》，把 AI 输出复制进提交物是不恰当的，作品必须是学生本人的；不确定时应询问。
coursework.meaningEn: Four-level framework and misconduct policy s4.2-4.5.
coursework.meaningZh: 四级框架与学术不端政策第 4.2–4.5 节。

exams.en: No university-wide AI permission for examinations was found; the applicable level is set in each assessment brief. Copilot access does not authorise exam use.
exams.zh: 未发现全校性的考试 AI 许可；适用等级由各项考核说明规定。能使用 Copilot 不代表考试获准使用。
exams.meaningEn: Assessment-specific; no general exam rule.
exams.meaningZh: 按考核规定；无一般考试规则。

disclosure.en: Students must acknowledge any generative AI use in coursework with a declaration statement alongside the references, unless the assessment brief gives other wording: either that no part was generated by AI (grammar and spell checking is consistent with this) or that parts have AI contributions within the brief's acceptable use, naming the tools and how they were used. AI is not cited as an authoritative source. Doctoral students choose one of two AI declarations on the RD2 form.
disclosure.zh: 学生须在课程作业的参考文献处附声明，说明生成式 AI 的使用情况（考核说明另有措辞的除外）：要么声明没有任何部分由 AI 生成（使用语法和拼写检查与此一致），要么声明部分内容有 AI 参与且符合考核说明的可接受范围，并写明工具及用途。AI 不作为权威来源引用。博士生须在 RD2 表格中选择两种 AI 声明之一。
disclosure.meaningEn: Coursework declaration and RD2 form.
disclosure.meaningZh: 课程作业声明与 RD2 表格。

privacy_data.en: Students should not input personal data, sensitive information or content created by others into any AI platform, even though King's Copilot has commercial data protection. Doctoral students must discuss confidentiality, copyright, data protection and ethics with their supervisors and get written approval before uploading any part of their research. Staff must not upload student work or details to AI tools without explicit permission.
privacy_data.zh: 即使国王学院的 Copilot 有商业数据保护，学生也不应向任何 AI 平台输入个人数据、敏感信息或他人创作的内容。博士生在上传研究项目任何部分前，须与导师团队讨论保密、版权、数据保护和伦理问题并取得书面批准。教职员工未经明确许可不得把学生作品或信息上传到 AI 工具。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Student guidance, doctoral upload approval and marking guidance.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 学生指引、博士上传审批与评分指引。

approved_tools.en: All King's students and staff can use Microsoft Copilot text and image generation by signing in with their KCL Microsoft account; the Enterprise licence provides commercial data protection. King's does not describe Copilot as the only or required tool, and access does not authorise its use in a particular assessment.
approved_tools.zh: 国王学院全体学生和员工可用 KCL 微软账号登录使用 Microsoft Copilot 的文本和图像生成；企业许可提供商业数据保护。学校并未把 Copilot 描述为唯一或必须使用的工具，能使用也不代表获准在某项考核中使用。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Context and student guidance.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 背景与学生指引。

research_publication.en: Doctoral students may use AI in an assistive role to clarify their own writing, including rewriting or paraphrasing parts of the thesis, but not to replace their authorship; AI in the research process itself (e.g. data analysis) falls under research design and ethics review. Uploading research material needs prior written supervisory approval, theses carry an RD2 AI declaration, and examiners must not upload theses to AI or use AI detectors.
research_publication.zh: 博士生可将 AI 作为辅助工具澄清自己的写作，包括改写或意译论文部分内容，但不能替代本人的作者身份；研究过程中的 AI（如数据分析）属于研究设计和伦理审查范畴。上传研究材料须事先取得导师团队书面批准，论文须附 RD2 AI 声明，评审人不得把论文上传到 AI 或使用 AI 检测工具。
research_publication.meaningEn: Doctoral assessment guidance.
research_publication.meaningZh: 博士考核指引。

academic_integrity.en: Inappropriate, unattributed AI use can be academic misconduct, but poor academic practice (e.g. incomplete citation) is not misconduct. Cases normally start with an informal Academic Integrity Meeting where students may be asked to explain their work but need not give specific answers. A Stage One penalty can be contested within 10 working days of written notification; a Misconduct Committee decision can be appealed within 10 working days on limited grounds. Outcomes range from warnings and capped resubmission to suspension or expulsion. King's has not enabled Turnitin's AI-detection percentage, though similarity checking continues.
academic_integrity.zh: 不当且未注明的 AI 使用可构成学术不端，但不规范的学术做法（如引用不完整）不属于不端。案件通常从非正式的学术诚信会议开始，学生可能被要求解释作品，但无义务给出特定回答。第一阶段处罚可在书面通知后 10 个工作日内提出异议；不端委员会决定可在 10 个工作日内基于有限理由上诉。处理结果从警告、限分重交到停学或开除不等。国王学院未启用 Turnitin 的 AI 检测百分比，但相似性检查仍在使用。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Academic Misconduct Policy s6.4, 7.4-7.35.

do.en: Check the assessment brief for the AI level (Minimal, Limited, Open or Embedded) and ask if uncertain.
do.zh: 查看考核说明中的 AI 等级（Minimal、Limited、Open 或 Embedded），不确定时询问。

do.en: Add the AI declaration statement with your references (no-AI or AI-contribution version, naming tools and uses).
do.zh: 在参考文献处附 AI 声明（未使用 AI 或有 AI 参与的版本，写明工具和用途）。

do.en: Doctoral students: get written supervisory approval before uploading research material, and complete the RD2 AI declaration.
do.zh: 博士生：上传研究材料前取得导师团队书面批准，并填写 RD2 AI 声明。

dont.en: Do not copy AI-generated output into a submission as your own or let AI make substantive changes to your work.
dont.zh: 不要把 AI 生成的输出当作自己的成果复制进提交物，也不要让 AI 对作品作实质性修改。

dont.en: Do not input personal data, sensitive information or other people's content into any AI platform.

dont.zh: 不要把能使用 Copilot 当作某项考核的使用许可。

CL-001.text: King's College London does not ban the use of generative AI by students. Whether and how AI may be used in a given assessment is set by the assessment guidance: students should be given clear guidance on the level of AI that is appropriate and should ask if uncertain.

evidence.quote: No, King's does not ban the use of any type of AI. It is increasingly part of the wider world and is changing the nature of many aspects of life including the jobs you are in or will progress into.
evidence.location: Is generative AI banned at King's?; lines 194-194 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You should be given clear guidance on what level of generative AI is appropriate in any given assessment. Things are moving quickly so if you are uncertain, please do ask.
evidence.location: What constitutes appropriate use?; lines 260-260 of captured page text

CL-002.text: At King's College London, inappropriate use of generative AI without attribution is considered academic misconduct and can result in penalties ranging from formal warnings to expulsion.

evidence.quote: Inappropriate use without attribution is considered academic misconduct. For further details please see the Academic Misconduct Policy and Academic Misconduct Procedure. Potential penalties can range from formal warnings, resubmitting the coursework, suspension or expulsion.
evidence.location: Student guidance > What are the consequences of inappropriate use of generative AI?

CL-003.text: King's College London does not require students to cite generative AI as an authoritative source in the reference list, but it requires students to acknowledge any use of generative AI tools in coursework by including a declaration statement with their references. Unless the assessment brief gives other wording, students append either a declaration that no part of the submission was generated by AI software (English grammar and spell checking is consistent with this statement) or a declaration that parts of the submission have AI contributions within the acceptable use specified in the brief, naming the tools and how they were used.

evidence.quote: King’s College London, unlike some other universities, does not require students to reference generative AI as an authoritative source in the reference list for much the same reason you would not be expected to cite a search engine, a student essay website or be over-dependent on synoptic, secondary source material.
evidence.location: How do I acknowledge use of generative AI?; lines 320-320 of captured page text

evidence.quote: King's requires students to acknowledge any use of generative AI tools in coursework by including a declaration statement along with your references. Please note that so long as acknowledged use falls within the scope of appropriate use as defined in the assessment brief/guidance then this will not have any direct impact on the grades awarded. Unless alternative wording is suggested in an assessment brief then you should append one of the following:
evidence.location: How do I acknowledge use of generative AI?; lines 324-324 of captured page text

evidence.quote:
1. I declare that no part of this submission has been generated by AI software. These are my own words. 

Note. Using software for English grammar and spell checking is consistent with Statement 1.
evidence.location: Declaration statement 1; lines 326-328 of captured page text

evidence.quote: 2. I declare that parts of this submission has contributions from AI software and that it aligns with acceptable use as specified as part of the assignment brief/ guidance and is consistent with good academic practice. The content can still be considered as my own words. I understand that as long as my use falls within the scope of appropriate use as defined in the assessment brief/guidance then this declaration will not have any direct impact on the grades awarded.
evidence.location: Declaration statement 2; lines 332-332 of captured page text

CL-004.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy states that using generative AI tools to produce output that is then copied as part of a submission is not appropriate, that any work submitted must genuinely demonstrate the student's own work, skills and knowledge and follow the assessment guidelines, and that generative AI writing programmes are third-party technologies to be used only in accordance with College guidance. The King's guidance adds that submitting AI-generated text as one's own without written departmental permission is considered misconduct (third-party involvement or text manipulation) where it gives undue advantage or interferes with assessment of the student's own understanding. A written permission or acknowledgement does not by itself make substantive AI content creation acceptable.

evidence.quote: However, the use of generative AI tools to produce output which is then copied as part of a submission is not appropriate. Prudent, ethical and constructive use of tools is increasingly likely to form part of the production of assessed work.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s4.2; physical PDF page 4; lines 172-174 of captured PDF text

evidence.quote: This means that any work submitted must represent a genuine demonstration of the student’s own work, skills and subject knowledge, adheres to the guidelines of the assessment task, and respects the College’s value of academic integrity and honesty.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s4.2; physical PDF page 4; lines 176-179 of captured PDF text

evidence.quote: The service should not assist with substantive content creation or structuring of the assessment. Above all, third parties cannot make substantive changes which compromise the authorship of the text
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s4.3; physical PDF page 4; lines 185-187 of captured PDF text

evidence.quote: For the avoidance of doubt, generative Artificial Intelligence writing programmes are third party technologies and must only be used in accordance with College guidance.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s4.5; physical PDF page 4; lines 197-199 of captured PDF text

evidence.quote: Submitting text generated by technology/artificial intelligence as their own, without written permission from their department is considered misconduct under the offences of third-party involvement or text manipulation, if it provides undue advantage or interferes with assessment of the student's own understanding.
evidence.location: Guidance on academic integrity, attribution, detection; lines 204-204 of captured page text

CL-005.text: King's College London states it took the decision not to enable the AI-writing detection percentage in Turnitin because of concerns about reliability and false positives. This is not the same as switching off similarity checking: the Academic Misconduct Policy still allows staff to use TurnitinUK or other means to help detect academic misconduct. The current back-end Turnitin configuration was not independently tested.

evidence.quote: King’s took the decision not to enable the AI detection % in Turnitin due to concerns about its reliability and potential for false positives. As things stand AI detection is not an option that is available to us.
evidence.location: Detection; lines 210-210 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Staff may use the electronic software “TurnitinUK” or other means to assist them in the process of detecting academic misconduct.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s6.4; physical PDF page 6; lines 282-283 of captured PDF text

CL-007.text: King's College London states that its Enterprise licence means Copilot use comes with commercial data protection, making it a more secure alternative to other generative AI tools. Commercial data protection does not mean any data may be entered: King's student guidance says not to input personal data, sensitive information or content created by others into any AI platform.

evidence.quote: Our Enterprise license means that use of Copilot comes with commercial data protection and is therefore a more secure alternative to other generative AI tools.
evidence.location: Equity of access; lines 214-214 of captured page text

evidence.quote: You should not input personal data, sensitive information or content created by others into any AI platform.
evidence.location: What should I avoid?; lines 250-250 of captured page text

CL-009.text: King's College London permits doctoral students to use generative AI tools in an assistive role in thesis writing, to clarify their own writing and avoid misrepresenting their meaning; this can include rewriting, rephrasing or paraphrasing parts of the thesis. Use beyond the circumstances permitted by the doctoral guidance risks breaching the Academic Misconduct Policy, and AI used in the research process itself (for example to analyse data) is largely outside this guidance and falls under research design, ethical review and research-integrity norms.

evidence.quote: Yes, students are permitted to make use of generative AI tools in their thesis writing processes. However, where a student's use of generative AI tools in their thesis writing exceeds the circumstances permitted by this guidance, they will risk breaching the Academic Misconduct Policy.
evidence.location: Are students allowed to use generative AI tools when writing their thesis?; lines 168-170 of captured page text

evidence.quote: Doctoral students can use generative AI tools in an assistive role to clarify their own writing and help ensure that their own meaning is not misrepresented due to the quality and standard of the English used. This may go beyond simply correcting spelling and basic grammar, and can involve the rewriting, rephrasing and/or paraphrasing parts of the thesis.
evidence.location: Assistive use; lines 218-218 of captured page text

evidence.quote: The use of AI tools as part of the research process – to analyse and draw insights from data, for example – is therefore largely beyond the scope of this guidance. At a minimum, such usage would, like any other element of research design, be clearly outlined by authors in a ‘Methods’ section, subject to ethical review where appropriate, and conducted in accordance with principles of research integrity as well as disciplinary norms.
evidence.location: Scope; lines 204-204 of captured page text

CL-010.text: King's College London doctoral examiners must not upload any part of a student's thesis into a generative AI tool or use external AI detection software when assessing the thesis.

evidence.quote: Must not upload any part of a student's thesis into a generative AI tool, or make use of external generative AI detection software when assessing the thesis.
evidence.location: Doctoral assessment > Principles for generative AI use by doctoral researchers at King's > Examiners

CL-011.text: King's College London suggests four broad levels of generative AI use in assessment that programme and module leaders may adjust to each assessment: Minimal (routine tools such as auto transcription, spell and grammar checkers), Limited/selective (clearly delineated tasks as allowed), Open (no specific restrictions but key stages and tools must be tracked) and Embedded (AI use is a focal part of the assessment). The levels are a framework for the actual assessment brief, not an automatic university-wide permission, and verbatim use of generated content without acknowledgement is never appropriate.

evidence.quote: We have suggested four broad levels that your Programme and Module leaders may adjust to the specifics of an assessment:

evidence.quote: Once again, we state that in no circumstance is it appropriate to use generated content verbatim without clear indication and acknowledgement, or to effectively outsource the writing task as much as it is inappropriate to get someone else to write something and claim it as your own.

draft-claim-kcl-academic-integrity-meeti.text: Under King's Academic Misconduct Policy, a suspected case normally goes first to a Stage One Academic Integrity Meeting (AIM) with two staff members. The AIM is not a hearing and should be informal, supportive and exploratory; where authorship or third-party involvement is in doubt the student may be asked to explain their answers, ideas or references, but must not be pressured or obliged to give specific responses and may respond in writing instead. Staff share their notes, and the student may add information, normally within 5 working days. Possible Stage One outcomes are no concern, poor academic practice, a local educative or restorative outcome, or referral to a Stage Two Misconduct Committee.

evidence.quote: The student will be invited to attend the Academic Integrity Meeting (AIM), which will normally be with any two of the following staff members: module leader, programme leader (or deputy), ASB Chair (or nominee), Programme Manager or personal tutor.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy s7.7-7.8; physical PDF page 8; lines 392-395 of captured PDF text

draft-claim-kcl-misconduct-contestation-.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy provides two different review routes with different start points. Where a Stage One AIM finds misconduct and applies a local penalty (Outcome 3), the student may send a contestation in writing to Student Conduct & Appeals within 10 working days from the date of written notification of the Stage One outcome. A Stage Two Misconduct Committee decision may be appealed, on the grounds of new evidence or significant procedural error, by submitting a Misconduct Appeal Form within 10 working days of the date of the Misconduct Committee outcome. Possible outcomes range from educative measures such as a formal warning or capped resubmission to punitive outcomes up to suspension or expulsion; AI use does not carry an automatic penalty.

draft-claim-kcl-poor-academic-practice.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes poor academic practice from academic misconduct: an ASB Chair may decide a concern is an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice (for example incomplete citation), which is not misconduct; the student receives feedback and the work is marked against the criteria. Blatant, extensive or careless failures are excluded from this category.

evidence.quote: Once the ASB Chair (or their nominee) has reviewed the information available, they may decide that the concern relates to poor academic practice and that no academic misconduct has occurred. Poor academic practice involves an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice. Examples include when sources are acknowledged to some extent, but citation is inadequate or incomplete. It does not include when the failure to adhere to scholarly practice is blatant, extensive or results from a lack of effort. Poor academic practice is not a form of academic misconduct.

claim-snu-002a.text: SNU's AI Guidelines present voluntary principles rather than uniform prohibitions or restrictions on AI use, supporting context-specific judgment, creative approaches, and clear communication grounded in academic autonomy, trust, and social responsibility.
claim-snu-002a.scope: All intramural members (faculty, students, researchers, developers, administrative staff) and SNU-led collaborations

evidence.quote:
The purpose of these Guidelines is to set forth principles for the appropriate use of AI across
education and learning, research and development, and administrative functions, and to issue
recommendations for putting those principles into practice. Rather than imposing uniform
prohibitions or restrictions on AI use, the Guidelines are intended to support context-specific
judgment, creative approaches, and clear communication. The use of AI should respect the
autonomy of University members, grounded in the trust that underpins the University’s academic
community, and should be carried out in a manner that harmonizes creative scholarly activity with
social responsibility.

topicBasis.coursework: SNU's AI Guidelines do not impose uniform coursework bans. Under Chapter 2 §2(1)–(2), instructors should determine permitted and prohibited AI use and reporting methods according to course nature and should clearly state them in syllabi. Under §2(5)–(6), students must review and comply with syllabus policies, must report AI use when required, and bear final responsibility for their work. Campus ChatGPT Edu or Codex access does not grant coursework permission.
topicBasis.exams: Under Chapter 2 §2(3), except where AI use is explicitly permitted under course policies, instructors should take care to prevent students from gaining unfair advantages in assignments or examinations through improper AI use, while understanding the limitations and imperfections of AI detection tools. Under §2(7), using AI in ways prohibited by the instructor may be deemed an academic ethics violation and may result in academic or disciplinary disadvantages.
topicBasis.disclosure: Members should share and appropriately acknowledge AI use to the extent possible (§1(1)). For coursework, students must report AI use in the prescribed manner when required by the instructor's syllabus policy (§2(5)). For research and scholarly writing, directly incorporating AI outputs without modification may violate field research integrity standards (§3(3)); under §3(3) Footnote 1, using AI solely for foreign-language expression correction or grammatical review does not in itself constitute research misconduct merely because it is undisclosed, provided that it does not violate the policies of funding agencies, affiliated institutions, academic societies, or scholarly journals (research-only rule, not a coursework exception).
topicBasis.privacy_data: Members must comply with copyright, privacy, and information security laws and University rules, ensuring prompts and inputs do not include personal information, copyrighted works, or rights-infringing content (§1(3)). In research, researchers must take care to prevent leakage of sensitive research information (R&D plans, research data, project information, and researcher personal data), should not unnecessarily enter or share research data or confidential information with AI tools (§3(4)), and must strictly observe research security laws. Separately, SNU Central Library warns that uploading subscribed e-resources to AI services or bulk scraping violates publisher license terms.
topicBasis.approved_tools: SNU provides ChatGPT Edu (with Codex software development support) from June 2026 to August 2027 (15 months) for currently enrolled students and employed faculty/researchers via batch registration, and administrative staff by individual application (members on academic or employment leave (휴학·휴직) are excluded; affiliated school teachers receive ChatGPT Plus by application). The SNU press release states ChatGPT Edu is free of charge for students and excludes user input/output data from model training; accounts inactive for 3+ months are recalled. Tool availability does not authorize coursework or exam use.
topicBasis.research_publication: Under Chapter 2 §3, researchers must review and cross-validate AI outputs against literature, experiments, and expert judgment (§3(2)); must lead core research design and interpretation rather than replacing scholarly judgment with AI (§3(6)); should record prompts, versions, model names, and scope to the extent possible for reproducibility (§3(5)); and must review and comply in advance with policies of funding agencies, affiliated institutions, academic societies, and scholarly journals (§3(7)). Under §3(3) Footnote 1, foreign-language expression or grammar editing without explicit disclosure does not in itself constitute research misconduct only provided those external/institutional policies are not violated. SNU Library also cites COPE rules that AI cannot be listed as an author.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Members bear full responsibility for submitted outputs (§1(6)) and should verify facts and sources (§1(2)). Under Chapter 2 §2(7), using AI in ways prohibited by the instructor may be deemed a violation of academic ethics (학습 윤리 위반으로 인정되어) and may result in academic or disciplinary disadvantages (불이익을 받을 수 있음), without establishing an automatic finding or sanction. Under §2(3), instructors should understand the limitations and imperfections of AI detection tools (no sole-evidence prohibition is stated). In research, unedited direct incorporation of AI output may violate field research integrity standards (§3(3)), and COPE guidance cited by the Library bars AI authorship.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Under Chapter 2 §2(1)–(4) and §2(8)–(9), all instructor and university teaching provisions use normative SHOULD recommendations: instructors should determine permitted/prohibited AI scope and reporting rules according to course nature (§2(1)), should clearly state and communicate policies in syllabi (§2(2)), should understand AI detection tool limitations and imperfections (§2(3)), and should avoid relying exclusively on AI when evaluating student performance (Korean: 지양한다, §2(4), not an absolute ban). The University should provide guidance/resources for syllabus policies (§2(8)) and should institutionally support alternative teaching and assessment methods not reliant on AI detection tools (§2(9), institutional recommendation SHOULD, not an individual student entitlement).
topicBasis.security_procurement: SNU's ChatGPT Edu deployment provides a high-security workspace where user input/output data are not used for model training. For subscribed electronic resources, SNU Central Library enforces publisher license contracts: uploading full text to commercial AI services or using automated scraping tools/robots via DOIs is prohibited regardless of copyright fair use, and repeated breaches may trigger university-wide access suspension, fee increases, and sanctions under Central Library Enforcement Rules Article 24. Internal IT vendor procurement review criteria were not independently established in the reviewed sources.

do.en: Acknowledge AI use following University Library guidance: cite direct text/image use formally, provide an overview acknowledgement when asked or appropriate, and include prompts/outputs in an appendix when referencing AI as personal communication or required by School instructions.

do.en: Use your University IT account to access Microsoft Copilot Chat for commercial data protection; if uploading taught session recordings for study assistance, use University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot (DocID 79331 §2.2.2).

topicBasis.coursework: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.1.1, assessments are categorized into four levels (Category A: AI Prohibited, Category B: AI Minimal, Category C: AI Permitted, Category D: AI-Integrated) by Course Unit Directors and clearly stated in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3). Students may choose not to use AI for Categories A, B, and C without disadvantage, but this choice does not apply to Category D assessments which assess AI learning outcomes (§2.1.2). In Category A, all AI use including proofreading and text editing is prohibited; in Category B, AI is restricted to presentation only (fluency, grammar, spelling, formatting) without altering student ideas, arguments, or conclusions.
topicBasis.exams: Examinations and timed assessments are categorized individually under the four-category framework (DocID 79331 §2.1.1). Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §3.1.2.5 and §4.3.1, students must adhere strictly to examination conditions communicated before the exam, and possessing or using unauthorized AI tools or online materials in examination sittings constitutes academic malpractice.
topicBasis.disclosure: Under University Library referencing guidance, students must cite generative AI tools when using text or images directly in their work following 'Cite them Right' conventions. Where asked or deemed appropriate, students should include an overview acknowledgement at the start of work or in a footnote. An appendix detailing relevant prompts, outputs, generation dates, and modification statements is required when referencing AI as personal communication or when instructed by School guidance. Using tools for basic grammar and spell checking does not require acknowledgement unless School guidance requires it.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c), students must not upload University-owned copyright materials (such as lecture recordings, slides, handouts, or examination questions) to external commercial AI tools. Under §2.2.2, students are explicitly permitted to upload session recordings into University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot for study support. Under §2.3.1, staff members who use AI in Teaching and Learning activities must adhere to the University's AI Guidelines, and only the University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot service may be used for student-identifiable or confidential data.
topicBasis.approved_tools: The University provides Microsoft Copilot Chat with Commercial Data Protection to all active students and staff using University credentials. Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is deploying in phased license cohorts across 65,000 colleagues and students. NebulaONE is provided as an enterprise cloud AI development sandbox. Under DocID 79331 §2.1.1 and §2.2.1, having access to institutional AI tools does not confer permission to use them in Category A assessments.
topicBasis.research_publication: Under StaffNet Research Guidelines, any use of AI to synthesise research data must be completely transparent, and fabricating or falsifying data with AI constitutes research misconduct. Corresponding authors carry ultimate responsibility for publication credibility and must declare significant AI assistance. Researchers reviewing papers or grants must preserve peer review confidentiality and never upload unpublished manuscripts into external AI services.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Senate Policy DocID 79331 and Faculty guidance mandate that Course Unit Directors specify AI categories in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3), establish group work logging rules and require prior peer consent before recording group discussions (§2.1.4–2.1.5), and require teaching staff handling student-identifiable data to use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1). Faculty guidance (FSE, BMH) supplements central policy.
topicBasis.security_procurement: IT Services and Information Governance establish clear tenant boundaries for Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and NebulaONE cloud sandbox, ensuring user authentication, commercial data encryption, and exclusion of university data from public LLM training.

do.en: Check the specific Moodle statement (Without Limits, Guided, or Must Not Be Used) before using AI.
do.zh: 在开始每项作业前，务必核对 Moodle 标注的标准 AI 声明（无限制、引导使用或严禁使用）。

do.en: Follow task instructions, acknowledge the AI tool and its contribution, cite when necessary, and acknowledge non-use if AI was permitted but unused.
do.zh: 遵循任务说明，书面注明所用 AI 及贡献程度，必要时引用；任务允许但未使用 AI 时也应声明未使用。

do.en: Use Monash enterprise logins for commercial data protection and protect confidential research and personal data.
do.zh: 使用莫纳什官方账号激活商业数据保护，严禁向外部 AI 工具上传个人隐私、版权课件或机密科研数据。

dont.en: Do not treat campus Microsoft Copilot or Google Gemini access as coursework assessment permission.
dont.zh: 不要把学校提供的 Copilot 或 Gemini 账号权限当作课程作业的使用许可。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI or unapproved browser plugins in scheduled eExams unless authorized on landing page.
dont.zh: 严禁在电子期末考试（eExam）中使用生成式 AI 或未授权插件，除非考试首页明确允许。

dont.en: Do not use AI to rewrite text or change words under the guise of proofreading (§4.6).
dont.zh: 严禁以润色为名利用 AI 重写段落、换词或生成实质内容（润色仅限于识别拼写和语法错漏，§4.6）。

scope.en: Monash University delegates assessment conditions to Chief Examiners via four standard Moodle statements (§1.7.1–1.7.2). Enterprise Copilot and Gemini access is not assessment permission. Proofreading is strictly limited to identifying spelling and grammar errors (§4.6), AI detection software is barred from misconduct evidence, and unacknowledged use is a breach under §4.7.
scope.zh: 莫纳什大学依据《考核制度程序》§1.7.1–1.7.2 由课程主任通过四类标准 Moodle 声明设定 AI 规则。校方企业级 Copilot 与 Gemini 权限不构成考核许可。润色仅严格限于拼写与语法错漏识别（§4.6），AI 检测工具严禁作为不端证据，未声明使用属于违规行为（§4.7）。

proposed:uapt-monash-20261021-cl-020.text: Under Student Academic Integrity Procedure, minor, trivial or frivolous breaches due to inappropriate academic practice receive the educative response in §6.1: the Chief Examiner/RO/nominee provides support and a written warning outcome, and awards a mark reflecting the practice without imposing a penalty (§6.1.1). For alleged misconduct, where evidence was not provided with the notice of allegation, students must have a reasonable opportunity of not less than five working days to respond to the allegation and evidence before RO determination (§8.3). Invited students may bring a support person who cannot represent or advocate; at Monash Malaysia a staff member or student may represent them (§8.4). Under §11.1, a finding and penalty, or penalty alone, may be appealed; students who admitted the misconduct may appeal only the penalty. The Hearing and Appeals Panels Procedure governs that process. At Malaysia, §11.2 separately permits a written appeal to the Malaysian Registrar General within 14 days of receiving the decision. Where an academic misconduct allegation occurs WITH a research misconduct allegation, §7.6 instead refers the matter to the research-misconduct RO and this coursework procedure does not investigate or determine it.

topicBasis.coursework: Under Assessment Regime Procedure V12 §1.7–1.7.2 and Table 2, Chief Examiners must determine where and how generative AI can be used in a unit or assessment task, clearly publish use specifications in the required LMS section before the teaching period or at least 4 weeks before task details are released (with Table 2 noting a 4-week deadline before the due date / timetable release), and provide educational reasoning when AI is disallowed. Every Moodle assessment task displays one of four standard AI statements.
topicBasis.exams: In all scheduled electronic examinations (eExams), generative AI is strictly prohibited unless explicit permission is granted by the Chief Examiner and displayed on the eExam landing page. Online spell check, grammar, and translation tools are also barred in closed-book and non-open-access exams.
topicBasis.disclosure: When AI use is allowed or required in an assessment, follow its instructions and restrictions, document the type of AI and its contribution, and provide written acknowledgement of use and extent. Cite and reference using the closest appropriate source type when necessary. If AI is permitted but unused, acknowledge non-use. Further tool, version or prompt documentation follows the actual task instructions; no universal prompt-history requirement is established by the cited assessment-use rule.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Monash provides student access to Microsoft Copilot (with commercial data protection via Monash login) and Google Gemini / NotebookLM (opt-in for students 18+). Queries on enterprise accounts are not used to train foundational AI models. However, tool access does not confer coursework assessment permission, and users must avoid uploading personal, sensitive, copyrighted, or confidential data.
topicBasis.approved_tools: Monash provides institutional access to Microsoft Copilot and opt-in Google Gemini/NotebookLM for students aged 18 and over. The tool directory also lists Zoom AI Companion. Other enterprise-service eligibility is not independently established here; institutional access does not grant assessment permission, which follows the Chief Examiner’s task instructions.
topicBasis.research_publication: HDR students should discuss intended GenAI use and acknowledgement with supervisors. At progress management reviews they are asked about use and must confirm consistency with Monash policies/guidance and acknowledgement. Thesis submission forms and preliminary pages prompt AI disclosure. Thesis examiners must not use GenAI to support, prepare or write their reports.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Under Student Academic Integrity Procedure, minor, trivial or frivolous breaches due to inappropriate academic practice receive the educative response in §6.1: the Chief Examiner/RO/nominee provides support and a written warning outcome, and awards a mark reflecting the practice without imposing a penalty (§6.1.1). For alleged misconduct, where evidence was not provided with the notice of allegation, students must have a reasonable opportunity of not less than five working days to respond to the allegation and evidence before RO determination (§8.3). Invited students may bring a support person who cannot represent or advocate; at Monash Malaysia a staff member or student may represent them (§8.4). Under §11.1, a finding and penalty, or penalty alone, may be appealed; students who admitted the misconduct may appeal only the penalty. The Hearing and Appeals Panels Procedure governs that process. At Malaysia, §11.2 separately permits a written appeal to the Malaysian Registrar General within 14 days of receiving the decision. Where an academic misconduct allegation occurs WITH a research misconduct allegation, §7.6 instead refers the matter to the research-misconduct RO and this coursework procedure does not investigate or determine it.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Chief Examiners set unit assessment conditions; AI detectors are barred from breach evidence; markers must use similarity detection (Turnitin) and academic judgement.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Under AI Operations Procedure §1.3, decisions affecting rights/interests require human staff review and accountability; non-procured systems prohibited.

do.en: Get express permission from your instructor, supervisor, or program before using GenAI in assessed work, and check the course syllabus statement (Senate V-130 / O-130.1).
do.zh: 在评分考核作品中使用生成式 AI 前必须获得授课教师、导师或项目明确许可，并查阅课程大纲中的 GenAI 说明条款（参议院 V-130 / O-130.1）。

do.en: Follow course acknowledgement rules when AI is permitted, and in UBC Vancouver Graduate School theses declare each AI tool and purpose in the Preface (or state non-use).
do.zh: 在获准使用 AI 的课程中遵守标注规范；在 UBC 温哥华校区研究生院学位论文前言中列明每种工具与用途（或明确声明未使用）。

do.en: Check purpose-specific UBC privacy approval; in instructor-required course use of Copilot for Organizations, required student inputs are limited to U1 Low Risk information.
do.zh: 核实符合具体用途的 UBC 隐私审批；教师强制课程使用 Copilot for Organizations 时，可要求学生输入的内容限于 U1 低风险信息。

dont.en: Do not enter personal, confidential, or student grading data into uncleared AI tools, and do not require students to sign up for ChatGPT 5 with an account in a course.
dont.zh: 切勿将个人信息、机密资料或学生成绩输入未经 PIA 审批的 AI 工具，且不得在课程中强制要求学生注册使用 ChatGPT 5 有账号版本。

dont.en: Do not treat institutional access to Copilot Chat (Basic) or CTLT low-risk PIA status for ChatGPT 5 (Without An Account) as permission to use AI on assessed work.
dont.zh: 切勿将机构的 Copilot Chat（Basic）访问权限或 CTLT 对 ChatGPT 5（无账号版）的低风险 PIA 状态视作可在考核作业中使用 AI 的许可。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in examinations or assignments without express permission; unauthorized use is subject to Academic Calendar misconduct and §11 appeal rules.
dont.zh: 未经明确许可切勿在考试或作业中使用生成式 AI；违规使用将按《大学历书》学术不端规章及第 11 节申诉程序处理。

clm-ubc-academic-misconduct-appeal-vanco.text: Under UBC Vancouver Academic Calendar §11 (Appeals to the Senate Committee on Student Appeals on Academic Discipline), the applicable rules depend on the date on which the alleged act of misconduct took place: under the rules governing all appeals involving allegations of misconduct occurring on or after August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2), a student wishing to appeal a disciplinary decision made by the President must do so within 45 calendar days from the date the student receives the President's letter informing the student of the President's decision by submitting a written appeal to the Registrar that gives a full explanation of the grounds for the appeal and contains all documents the student intends to rely upon (with Registrar discretion to extend the appeal time limit if the Registrar determines an extension is appropriate); under the historical rules governing allegations of misconduct occurring prior to August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2), the Registrar must receive written notification giving a full explanation of the grounds within 45 calendar days of the date of the President's letter (with Registrar discretion to extend if, in the Registrar's opinion, circumstances warrant). For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. The reviewed Okanagan page has separate before/after headings but does not independently establish mixed-date case handling.

clm-ubc-academic-misconduct-appeal-okana.text: Under UBC Okanagan Academic Calendar §11 (Appeals to the Senate Committee on Appeals of Standing and Discipline), two distinct rule regimes apply depending on whether the alleged misconduct occurred on/after or prior to August 1, 2019: under the rules governing all appeals involving allegations of misconduct occurring on or after August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2), a student wishing to appeal a disciplinary decision made by the President must do so within 45 calendar days from the date the student receives the President's letter informing the student of the President's decision by submitting a written appeal to the Registrar that gives a full explanation of the grounds for the appeal and contains all documents the student intends to rely upon (with Registrar discretion to extend the appeal time limit if the Registrar determines an extension is appropriate); under the historical rules governing allegations of misconduct occurring prior to August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2), the Registrar must receive written notification giving a full explanation of the grounds within 45 calendar days of the date of the President's letter (with Registrar discretion to extend if, in the Registrar's opinion, circumstances warrant). For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. The reviewed Okanagan page has separate before/after headings but does not independently establish mixed-date case handling.

For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. The reviewed Okanagan page has separate before/after headings but does not independently establish mixed-date case handling.

topicBasis.coursework: Students may only use generative AI for coursework and assignments if expressly permitted by their instructor or program. Effective September 1, 2026, Vancouver Senate Policy V-130 and Okanagan Senate Policy O-130.1 require syllabi for all credit-bearing courses (graduate-level theses and dissertation courses are exempt) to include a GenAI usage statement, provided within the first week of class unless the syllabus is created in consultation with the student(s) at the beginning of a course section (in which case it must be finalized prior to the last date to drop the course without receiving a 'W' on the transcript).
topicBasis.exams: Students must not use generative AI in examinations or other assessed work unless expressly permitted by their course instructor or program. University-wide uniform exam exemption rules were not identified in the specific reviewed UBC sources; assessment-level boundaries are set by instructors and unauthorized use is addressed as academic misconduct under the Vancouver and Okanagan Academic Calendars.
topicBasis.disclosure: Where GenAI is permitted in assessed coursework, educators specify when and how students must acknowledge its use. In the Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies (Graduate School) at UBC Vancouver (grad.ubc.ca), graduate students must obtain supervisor/committee approval for substantive GenAI use and must declare in the thesis or dissertation Preface each AI tool used and its purpose, or include a clear statement that generative AI was not deliberately used for any aspect of the work (UBCO College of Graduate Studies thesis preface specifications were not separately verified in reviewed sources).
topicBasis.privacy_data: Do not enter personal information into unapproved AI tools; student learning/grading data requires a PIA approved for that purpose. CTLT guidance concerns instructor-required course tool use, not voluntary student choice: it says instructors cannot require ChatGPT 5 with an account, and limits what students can be instructed to share with Copilot for Organizations to Standard U1 Low Risk information. Other Copilot use follows current authorized-purpose, privacy, security and records requirements.
topicBasis.approved_tools: UBC provides Copilot Chat (Basic) to eligible students, faculty, and staff via UBC credentials with enterprise data protection (prompts/responses not used to train foundation models). Launched October 15, 2026, M365 Copilot (Premium) is a paid annual Workday subscription for eligible faculty and staff only and is not available to students. Under CTLT PIA guidance for required course use (updated February 17, 2026), ChatGPT 5 (Without An Account) is assessed low risk for required course use with caution (though it does not protect personal information and shares data outside Canada), while ChatGPT 5 (With An Account) must not be required for a course. Tool access or PIA status never grants assessment permission. CTLT Low Risk input guidance is specifically about what instructors can require students to share in a course; it is not a blanket approval or restriction for every Premium use.
topicBasis.research_publication: In the Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies (Graduate School) at UBC Vancouver (grad.ubc.ca), substantive GenAI use in graduate research or thesis drafting requires prior supervisor/committee approval, and thesis/dissertation prefaces must name each tool used and explain its purpose or include a clear statement that GenAI was not deliberately used (UBCO College of Graduate Studies thesis preface specifications were not separately verified in reviewed sources). Across UBC, researchers and educators must respect Indigenous data sovereignty and obtain express community permission before entering Indigenous knowledges or data into AI tools.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: All GenAI use must adhere to Academic Misconduct regulations in the Vancouver and Okanagan Academic Calendars; AI content detectors are strongly discouraged and Turnitin AI detection is disabled. Under Academic Calendar §11 (Appeals), the applicable Senate appeal rules depend on the date on which the alleged act of misconduct took place: for allegations of misconduct occurring on or after August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.2, §11.4–§11.5), a student must submit a written appeal to the Registrar within 45 calendar days from the date the student receives the President's letter, giving a full explanation of the grounds and containing all documents the student intends to rely upon (with Registrar extension discretion if appropriate), heard by at least 5 committee members at Vancouver and at least 4 at Okanagan (unless the student consents to fewer), with written and oral submissions, legal counsel representation, and a support person; for allegations occurring prior to August 1, 2019 (§11.1–§11.3), the Registrar must receive written notification within 45 calendar days of the date of the President's letter and the student may be represented or assisted by any person, including legal counsel. For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. The reviewed Okanagan page has separate before/after headings but does not independently establish mixed-date case handling.
topicBasis.governance: Under BC FIPPA, UBC requires case-by-case Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) for university tools and initiatives handling personal information, and requires a dedicated PIA before any AI tool is used to enter student/learning data for feedback or grading. A single centralized public AI procurement registry was not identified in the specific reviewed UBC sources.
topicBasis.teaching: Faculty and staff may use GenAI in teaching and learning within legal, university, Faculty, and program-level boundaries. Effective September 1, 2026, Senate Policies V-130 (Vancouver) and O-130.1 (Okanagan) require syllabi for all credit-bearing courses (graduate-level theses and dissertation courses exempt) to include Academic Integrity and GenAI usage statements, provided within the first week of class unless created in consultation with the student(s) at the beginning of a course section (finalized prior to the drop-without-'W' deadline). Instructors must not upload student work or third-party copyright material to unapproved AI tools.

do.en: Check your school-specific policy and course syllabus before using generative AI in coursework: adhering schools under CSSI Standards & Discipline require prior instructor authorization, while Columbia Law School allows defined research/writing support by default unless the instructor restricts it.
do.zh: 在课程作业中使用生成式 AI 前，请核对所在学院具体规范及课程大纲：采纳 CSSI《学生纪律规范》的学院默认须获教师事先授权，而哥大法学院默认允许既定研究与写作辅助（教师另有要求除外）。

do.en: Disclose any generative AI use contributing to your work product as required by your school (mandatory at Columbia Law School §7; required under CBS Honor Code when permitted), and follow course citation protocols.
do.zh: 按所在学院要求如实披露协助完成学业成果的 AI 使用情况（哥大法学院第 7 条强制要求；商学院获批使用时依据荣誉准则必须规范引用），并遵守具体引注规范。

do.en: Check the exact data class, account, approved model and feature before entering research, client or health information; a product name or BAA alone is insufficient.
do.zh: 输入科研、客户或健康资料前，核对数据分类、具体账号及获批模型和功能；不能仅凭产品名称或 BAA 推定许可。

dont.en: Do not assume AI is permitted in an examination: follow your school and course rules, including written-permission conditions and Law School default-policy exceptions.
dont.zh: 不要假定考试允许使用 AI；须遵循所在学院和课程的规定，包括书面许可条件及法学院默认政策的例外。

dont.en: Do not submit AI-generated text as your own independent work; under Columbia Law School rules, submitting machine-translated drafts of non-English writing as original English work is expressly prohibited.
dont.zh: 严禁将 AI 生成的文本作为个人原创作品提交；在哥大法学院规范下，严禁将非英语写作的机器翻译草稿作为原创英语成果提交。

dont.en: Do not enter Sensitive Data (PHI, PII, RHI) into tools lacking HIPAA BAAs like Workspace Gemini or unapproved commercial features, and do not use personal unvetted accounts for protected data.
dont.zh: 严禁将敏感数据（PHI、PII、RHI）输入缺乏 HIPAA BAA 的工具（如 Workspace 版 Gemini）或未经批准的商业功能，严禁使用个人未经审查的账户处理受保护数据。

scope.en: Covers Columbia University central Provost guidelines, CSSI Standards & Discipline 2026–2027 (adhering schools under Dean discretion), Columbia Law School 2026–2027 Default Academic Policy (with instructor written alternatives), Columbia Business School Honor Code, CUIMC Data Classification Matrix, and CUIT AI Services.

claim-columbia-004a.text: Under Columbia Law School's 2026–2027 Default Academic Policy on Student Use of AI (§9.1), use of AI during any examination is prohibited except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions; where not authorized, every word of an examination answer must be produced by the student without AI assistance (irrespective of whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten), and students are strictly forbidden from inputting current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns into an AI tool.
claim-columbia-004a.scope: Columbia Law School students in all JD, LLM, and JSD examinations

evidence.quote:
Examinations: Except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions, use of AI during any examination is prohibited.

- Every word of a student’s examination answer must be produced by that student without assistance from AI (including for English translation purposes). This prohibition encompasses all examinations, irrespective of format (i.e., whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten).

topicBasis.coursework: Under Columbia University's decentralized academic governance, coursework policies vary by school: schools adhering to CSSI Standards & Discipline (§C.3) treat unauthorized AI assistance as academic dishonesty requiring instructor written permission; Columbia Law School establishes a default permitting defined research and writing support unless the instructor alters it in writing (§8, §Default); and Columbia Business School requires following syllabus-designated assignment modes.
topicBasis.exams: Under both CSSI Standards & Discipline and Columbia Law School Policy (§9.1), generative AI is strictly prohibited on examinations unless advance written permission is granted by the instructor in the syllabus and/or examination instructions. For Columbia Law School examinations, inputting current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns into any AI tool is expressly prohibited across proctored, take-home, online, and handwritten formats.
topicBasis.disclosure: Columbia Law School (§7) imposes a mandatory requirement that students disclose any use of generative AI that contributes to a written submission or other work product, with an affirmative duty to err on the side of disclosure. At Columbia Business School, students must properly cite AI assistance according to Honor Code standards whenever AI is authorized. In adhering CSSI schools, students must follow the instructor's prescribed disclosure and citation protocols.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Follow the data classification and the exact account, model and feature approval. At CUIMC, Workspace Gemini/Gemini Notebook lack a HIPAA BAA and must not receive Sensitive Data; FERPA records can contain identifying/health elements requiring the stricter Sensitive Data treatment. CU AI Toolkit approval for PHI is limited to approved models, with all models in a shared chat history needing approval; approved Copilot products do not include every product using the Copilot brand. Public/unvetted tools must not receive confidential research material. Institutional tool availability is not assessment permission.
topicBasis.approved_tools: Columbia University officially endorses and provides several enterprise AI tools with data protection agreements: CUIT AI Toolkit (LibreChat, $0.15/day allowance for all UNIs), Google Gemini (Workspace, LionMail accounts), NotebookLM (Workspace note-taking), ChatGPT Education (procured via departmental chart string, $300/yr), Anthropic Claude for Education ($300/yr chart string), ChatGPT Enterprise (CUIMC clinical workforce), and Microsoft Copilot (CUIMC clinical HIPAA / CUIT M365 add-on). Critical governance principle: IT security clearance, Privacy Impact Assessments (PIA), and HIPAA BAA approvals establish technical data safeguards, but NEVER constitute academic assessment permission, which remains solely subject to the course syllabus.
topicBasis.research_publication: Under central Provost policy, researchers must not enter confidential research data, unpublished scholarly manuscripts, funding proposals, or research subject PII into public or unvetted AI tools, and using generative AI for peer review is strictly prohibited. Research analysis involving confidential or sensitive data must be conducted within CUIT-approved secure environments following IRB protocols, data use agreements, and sponsor requirements. At CUIMC, research protocol use involving Sensitive Data (including RHI) requires formal IRB submission and routing to the CUIMC AI Governance Committee (AIGC). Locally installed models require formal IT Risk Assessment.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Under Columbia University's Standards & Discipline (applicable to adhering schools at each Dean's discretion), unauthorized AI assistance is addressed through the Dean's Discipline process administered by CSSI. A report from an AI detection tool cannot be the sole piece of proof used to find a student responsible in a Dean’s Discipline case. Appeal timing under that process, subject to the recorded extension/final-notice qualifications, includes: 5 business days after receipt of the outcome letter, 5 business days for CSSI review, 2 business days from return for resubmission, and 10 business days from receipt for Dean review (with a 10 business day final notification qualifier from receipt). Under Columbia Law School default rules (§9.2, §11), submitted work must be student-composed, and submitting translated drafts of one's own non-English writing as original English work is prohibited by default (subject to written instructor alternatives).
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Faculty maintain primary pedagogical authority to define AI policies in course syllabi. Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) provides consultations and workshops for instructional design. Teachers College DFI provides five sample syllabus statements, including disability accommodations via OASID. Columbia Law School policy establishes default rules in Sections 8–11 that instructors may alter in writing in the course syllabus.
topicBasis.security_procurement: All institutional AI platforms must undergo CUIT security evaluation and procurement vetting under the central Data Classification Table to prevent model training on user submissions. At CUIMC, a formal IT Risk Assessment review is required before deploying any locally installed models to evaluate security, privacy, and healthcare compliance risks.

do.en: Check the UTOL assignment Permitted AI Use label (T0–T5 or Other) or course syllabus before using any generative AI tool.
do.zh: 使用任何生成式 AI 前，务必查阅 UTOL 作业页面上标注的「AI利用范围」标签（T0–T5 或 Other）或课程大纲说明。

do.en: Follow the instructor’s disclosure instructions; central guidance recommends asking students to name the AI tool used.
do.zh: 遵循教师的披露要求；中央指南建议教师要求学生注明使用的 AI 工具名称。

do.en: Use the institutional account specified for each service and check its data safeguards; no-training protection does not prove no retention.
do.zh: 使用各服务指定的机构账号并核对数据保护条件；不用于训练并不等于不留存。

dont.en: Never input personal information, confidential data, or unpublished research into AI tools; faculty must basically not input examination questions into language generation AI in unchanged form.
dont.zh: 切勿将个人信息、机密资料或未发表研究成果输入 AI 工具；教师原则上（基本的に）不得将考题以原样形式输入语言生成式 AI。

dont.en: Do not copy and paste AI-generated answers and submit them as your own work; unauthorized submission violates academic integrity.
dont.zh: 严禁将 AI 生成的解答全盘复制粘贴并作为原创作业提交；未授权提交构成学术不端。

dont.en: Do not assume institutional tool access (Copilot, Gemini, Zoom, Slack) grants permission to use AI in coursework or examinations.
dont.zh: 切勿将拥有校级 AI 工具访问权限（Copilot、Gemini、Zoom、Slack）误认为具备课程考核使用许可。

scope.en: UTOL LMS mandatory assignment Permitted AI Use setting (effective Sept. 29, 2026), Taura EVP 6-level taxonomy (T0–T5 / Other), instructor coursework discretion, disclosure recommendations, campus-wide Copilot and Gemini commercial data protection, and research misconduct procedure under Rule No. 79 (qualified in principle).
scope.zh: 涵盖 UTOL 教学管理系统作业必填「AI利用范围」设定（2026 年 9 月 29 日起生效）、田浦理事·副学长六级分类体系（T0–T5 及 Other）、教师平时作业裁量权、披露推荐规范、全校 Copilot 与 Gemini 商用数据保护，以及基于第 79 号规则的科学研究不端行为调查程序（设立原则时限）。

draft-u-tokyo-009.text: Under Rule No. 79 (東京大学科学研究行動規範委員会規則), formal scientific research misconduct investigations establish procedural timelines qualified in principle (原則として): the preliminary inquiry results must be reported to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving an allegation (Art. 8(5)); the Investigation Committee commences formal investigation in principle within 30 days of the decision to investigate (Art. 9(2)); the Committee makes its adjudication determination in principle within 150 days of starting formal investigation (Art. 11(1)); respondent defense opportunity is granted in principle within 14 days of receiving draft determination notification (Art. 11(7)); and a respondent against whom misconduct was determined may file an objection/appeal to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving the determination notice under Art. 11(11) (Art. 12(1)). These clocks apply exclusively to scientific research misconduct proceedings and do not govern undergraduate or generic coursework discipline.
draft-u-tokyo-009.scope: Scientific research activities and formal research misconduct investigations under Rule No. 79 (distinct from undergraduate/coursework discipline; all clocks qualified in principle)

evidence.quote: この規則は、科学研究に携わる東京大学(以下「本学」という。)の教職員及び本学の施設設備を利用して研究活動を行う者(以下「研究者」という。)を対象として、本学の科学研究における行動規範(以下「行動規範」という。)に違反する不正行為(過去に研究者であった者が、研究者であった時期に行った不正行為を含む。以下同じ。)に対処し、行動規範の遵守を促すための委員会の設置及び不正行為に対する措置等について定める。

topicBasis.coursework: On UTOL (UTokyo Online Learning), starting September 29, 2026, setting 'Permitted AI Use' is mandatory for all assignment creation. Course instructors must designate one of six standardized labels (T0 No AI Use; T1 questions/research only; T2 discussion/idea-bouncing; T3 feedback; T4 drafting; T5 creative use) or select 'Other' to provide specific written boundaries. Students must strictly adhere to the designated label for each assignment. Use only within the assignment’s stated permitted range; the reviewed guidance leaves course decisions to instructors.
topicBasis.exams: Follow the instructor’s explicit rules for each examination or test. The reviewed sources establish instructor discretion, not a university-wide written-authorization default. Faculty are advised basically (基本的に) not to input examination questions into language-generating AI in unchanged form because of confidentiality.
topicBasis.disclosure: Where generative AI tools are permitted in preparing reports or coursework assignments, course instructors are officially recommended to have students clearly specify which generative AI tools were used. Attribution practices and specific disclosure formats are determined at faculty discretion.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Under official faculty guidance and student notices, students and faculty are cautioned against information leakage: students must never input confidential information, personal data, or unpublished research results into AI tools due to potential leakage or model training use, and faculty are instructed that examination questions, being highly confidential documents, must basically (基本的に) not be input into language-generating AI in unchanged form. The separate 'Security Guidelines for Generative AI Use' (March 12, 2024) require internal UTokyo Account authentication and are held as an unverified private source.
topicBasis.approved_tools: U-Tokyo provides Google Gemini (via ECCS Cloud Email / Google Workspace) and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (via UTokyo Account) to university members with commercial data protection enabled. Zoom AI Companion is available under U-Tokyo Zoom licenses, and Slack AI is available in UTokyo Slack. Gemini for Google Workspace is available to users with Education Plus licenses. Tool licensing and data protection provide institutional account security, but NEVER confer permission to use tools in coursework or examinations, which is governed exclusively by instructor assignment instructions (T0–T5/Other).
topicBasis.research_publication: Under Rule No. 79 (東京大学科学研究行動規範委員会規則), formal scientific research misconduct investigations establish procedural timelines qualified in principle (原則として): the preliminary inquiry results must be reported to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving an allegation (Art. 8(5)); the Investigation Committee commences formal investigation in principle within 30 days of the decision to investigate (Art. 9(2)); the Committee makes its adjudication determination in principle within 150 days of starting formal investigation (Art. 11(1)); respondent defense opportunity is granted in principle within 14 days of receiving draft determination notification (Art. 11(7)); and a respondent against whom misconduct was determined may file an objection/appeal to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving the determination notice under Art. 11(11) (Art. 12(1)). The Code of Conduct for Research mandates transparent scientific basis and prohibits fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism. These clocks apply exclusively to scientific research misconduct proceedings and do not govern undergraduate or generic coursework discipline.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Do not present AI-generated work as your own. Faculty guidance says simply copying and pasting AI answers should not be accepted even where AI use is allowed. The reviewed sources do not establish a complete coursework investigation, penalty or appeal process; the gap remains open. Rule No.79 covers scientific research misconduct separately, with in-principle clocks; it must not supply coursework disciplinary steps.
topicBasis.teaching: Faculty members have broad discretion to set generative AI policy for their individual courses. Instructors are guided to test their own assignment prompts against generative AI models, clearly specify permitted use ranges using UTOL labels (T0–T5 or Other), not rely uncritically on AI detection tools due to false positive risks, and provide guidance on appropriate attribution.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Institutional IT strategy prioritizes commercial data protection through enterprise contracts with Microsoft (Copilot Chat) and Google (Gemini via ECCS Cloud Email and Education Plus). The separate 'Security Guidelines for Generative AI Use' (March 12, 2024) require internal UTokyo Account SSO sign-in; full text is held as an internal unverified source while public notices govern confidential, personal, and examination data safeguards.
